default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is Bill.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being worn.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: かけています describes the state of wearing glasses.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: は places the topic at the beginning of the sentence, while を connects to the object affected by the verb. かけています describes the current state of wearing glasses.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is still wearing glasses, but the expression is more general.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ています as "be doing" in every case, but here it emphasizes the state of wearing them.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: I put the gift inside the box.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the gift being put into the box.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 箱 with 中 to form the phrase "inside the box".
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the gift.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 入れました is the polite past form of 入れる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The gift comes before を because it is the item being moved. 箱の中に forms a location phrase, in which に marks the place where the gift is put.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence describes an action taking place inside the box, without emphasizing movement into it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に and で: に usually indicates a destination or a location of existence, while で usually indicates the place where an action takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 副詞 ＋ Amount ＋ Nでした
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents this shirt as the topic for comparison or comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょうど modifies the amount and shows that the price is exact.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 円 combines with a number to form a currency unit, while でした expresses a price in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: は makes the item being priced the topic. ちょうど comes before the amount to modify the price, and then でした ends the statement about the price.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ぐらい is used instead, the price only means about 1,000 yen and is no longer completely exact.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out 円 when reading an amount, but Japanese needs 円 to clearly show the unit yen.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: The restroom is in front of the stairs.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N の ＋ Location に ＋ あります
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the restroom is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun meaning stairs with the location in front.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the location where the restroom exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is used to talk about the existence of things or places that are not people.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The phrase かいだんの前に clearly states the location, and の creates the relationship "in front of the stairs." あります is suitable for a place or an inanimate object.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using であります sounds formal and unnatural in an ordinary sentence stating a location.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use います for a restroom; います is used for people and animals, while places and objects use あります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: When taking the train, you need a ticket.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the means of transport that the speaker gets on or travels by.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 乗るとき uses the dictionary form of a verb before とき to indicate the time before or during getting on the train.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the necessary item in the structure いります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いります is the predicate showing that the ticket is necessary.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: 乗るとき places the time condition before the main clause. In the main clause, きっぷ is the necessary item, so が is used with いります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: なら means "if you plan to take the train," emphasizing an assumption or topic rather than simply a time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: たら means "after getting on the train" or "if you get on the train," unlike とき, which means "when."
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with いります, but necessary items usually go with が: きっぷがいります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Vない形 ＋ とき
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: There are flowers blooming in the garden.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the flowers exist and bloom.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject in the state of blooming.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: さいています describes the flowers as being in bloom.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: 庭に states the location, while 花が is the subject of the state. The verb comes at the end of the sentence and uses ています to describe the flowers as being in bloom.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where an activity occurs, while に is more suitable for describing the existence or state of flowers in the garden.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: In a sentence describing an object that exists or is located somewhere, Vietnamese learners may easily use で instead of に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: Tanaka's mother is both beautiful and gentle.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states who is being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: きれい is the adjective な, changed to きれいで to connect it with the next adjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The topic comes before は, and the two qualities are connected with で. The final adjective takes です to end the polite sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: し states one reason or characteristic among several, with a stronger listing tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect きれいですやさしいです directly; they need to change きれいです to きれいで when connecting two adjectives.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q7.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or a polite title
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: I am going to bed. Good night.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.sk: N は ＋ もう ＋ Vます。 ＋ Greeting
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states who performs the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies 寝ます and shows that the action is about to happen or that it is time to do it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: This is a greeting used when ending the evening or before going to bed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: は identifies the speaker as the topic, while もう comes before the verb to show that the time has come. The next sentence is an independent greeting, separated by a period.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: まだ寝ません means that the speaker is still not going to bed, opposite to the intention of going to bed now in this sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: もう does not mean “anymore” in this sentence; it only shows that it is time to go to bed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ Number of people ＋ います
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed in the existence sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the existing people or the people that the subject has.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 四人 adds a quantity to 兄弟.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: います is used for people and animals to express existence or possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.cn: N は ＋ N が ＋ Quantity ＋ います／あります
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: The pattern ～は～がいます describes a person having someone else or someone else's existence. The quantity 四人 comes before います to show that there are four siblings.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression can still be understood as meaning that the speaker has four siblings, but it is less natural in basic conversation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Use います for people and animals; あります is used for objects and lifeless things.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vi: I have been to Kyoto once.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location, while は presents Kyoto as a topic for contrast or emphasis.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase modifies the experience of going to Kyoto and states the number of times.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたことが turns the verb into a noun, forming the part before あります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: あります completes the pattern for expressing past experience of doing something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: The place Kyoto is used with に and emphasized by は. The verb 行く changes to the た form before ことがある to express an experience that happened before.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 行きました, the sentence only says that the speaker went once at some time, without emphasizing the experience.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行ってみました is used, it means that the speaker tried going to Kyoto, emphasizing the attempt.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ことがある when talking about having done something before; use Vた.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vi: Every day, I go to school by this road.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.sk: Frequency + N を + Vて + N へ + Vます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The frequency phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and modifies the whole action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を shows the route that the speaker travels through, not the object of 通る.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 通る changes to the て form to connect the action of going through the road with the action of going to school.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement toward 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the main predicate and expresses the action of going to school.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: 道を通って describes the route traveled, and then へ shows the destination of 行きます. The て form connects two successive actions in the same sequence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with で, この道で emphasizes the place where the action happens, so it is less natural for describing the route traveled.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “along this road,” emphasizing following the road rather than going through or passing along it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for every place, but を in 道を通る shows the route traveled through.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being talked about as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the part that has the characteristic of being short.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 低い is an adjective ending in い and serves as the predicate, while です creates a polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: わたしは introduces the topic, while 背が shows the part that has the characteristic. The pattern NはNがAい describes a characteristic of a person or thing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If の背は is used, height is treated as the direct topic, so the focus is more on height.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 高くないです is used, the sentence gently and indirectly says that I am not tall, compared with 低いです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use を after 背 when describing a characteristic; the part that has the characteristic usually goes with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: I cooked with my younger brother.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と shows the person who performs the action together with the speaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いっしょに modifies the action 料理をしました and shows how it is performed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb しました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of します.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: The person acting together is connected with と, while the adverb いっしょに comes before the object and verb to express doing something together. 料理をしました forms the predicate showing that the action was completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it sounds more formal and can mean together with or at the same time as.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of と when talking about a person who performs an action together with them.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vi: When I arrive at the station, I will contact you.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the destination of the action 着く.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたら connects a conditional or time clause with the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 連絡します is the action performed after the condition in the preceding clause occurs.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: 駅に is the destination of 着く, and then 着いたら turns this clause into a time point or condition. The main action, 連絡します, is placed in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と, the sentence emphasizes a natural or inevitable result whenever one arrives at the station, so it is less suitable for the intention of contacting someone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なら, the sentence has a hypothetical tone or is based on information already mentioned about arriving at the station.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand たら as only meaning “when,” but this pattern can also express a condition meaning “if.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: The cafeteria over there is very good.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: あそこの modifies the noun that follows and shows its location or place of ownership.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the object 食堂 the topic for comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective おいしい serves as the predicate, and です creates a polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: あそこの comes before the noun to identify which cafeteria it is. The topic is introduced with は, and then おいしいです gives a comment about that topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes that cafeteria itself as the place that is good, instead of introducing the cafeteria as the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の after あそこ when using this word to modify a noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vi: I always work from Monday to Saturday.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies the verb and shows frequent occurrence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point of a period.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle まで shows the ending point of a period.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb きます forms a polite predicate in the present or future tense.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: いつも comes before the whole verb phrase to show a habit. から and まで form a pair that limits the time from the starting point to the ending point.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, the sentence only indicates the time of working on Monday, not a period of time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If にかけて is used, the period is described more broadly and less precisely.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use まで for both endpoints, but the starting point must use から.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: It is especially cold today, isn't it?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents today as the time being commented on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: とくに modifies 寒い and emphasizes the degree of coldness.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 寒い is an adjective ending in い and serves as the predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね comes at the end of the sentence to seek agreement or share an impression with the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: 今日 is made the topic with は, while とくに comes directly before 寒い to add emphasis about the degree. ですね ends the sentence with a shared comment and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If とくに is replaced with とても, the sentence only expresses a very high degree of coldness and does not emphasize that it is unusual compared with other days.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If ですね is replaced with でしょう, the sentence leans toward guessing or mild confirmation instead of sharing an impression.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place とくに after 寒い, but this adverb usually comes before the word or phrase being emphasized.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi: I cannot clearly understand the way. Let's look at the map together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that is or is not clearly understood.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies わかりません and shows the degree of understanding or recognition.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりません is the polite negative form of わかります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ね is used at the end of the sentence to share or confirm an impression with the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the map as the object being viewed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: 見ましょう is the polite volitional form, used to suggest doing an action together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: 道が is the thing being understood in the sentence わかりません, while よく shows the degree of understanding. In the next sentence, 図を is the object of 見ましょう, and the form ましょう makes a suggestion to do something together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If か is used, the sentence becomes a direct question asking whether the listener does not understand the way.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見ましょう is replaced with 見ませんか, the suggestion sounds softer and asks for the listener's opinion.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with わかる, but something that is understood or not understood usually goes with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: Is this a dish made from beef?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the thing being asked about as the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the ingredient with the noun りょうり, giving the meaning “a dish made from beef.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ですか forms a question confirming the identity or quality of the dish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: これは places the topic at the beginning of the sentence, while 牛肉の modifies りょうり to show the ingredient. ですか comes at the end to ask for confirmation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the sentence emphasizes that the dish is made with beef rather than simply stating the type of dish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle の and say 牛肉りょうり as one phrase, but の is needed to connect the two nouns.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: I want to travel during the summer vacation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.sk: Time に + N が + Vたいです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the time when the wish to travel takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the activity that is desired in the pattern Vがしたい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: したい is the “want to do” form of する, expressing the speaker's desire.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます + たいです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: 夏休みに places the time before the desired content. 旅行がしたい uses the noun 旅行 together with する, then changes する into したい to express a desire.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the sentence emphasizes wanting to go somewhere or take a trip, rather than simply talking about travel as an activity in general.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with したい, but in this pattern the desired activity usually goes with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vi: This store has many foreign goods.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents this store as the topic of comparison or comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 外国 with 品物, identifying the origin or type of the goods.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing being described as numerous.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is an i-adjective used as the predicate to describe the amount of goods.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: この店は sets the scope of the comment, and 外国の品物が is the thing that exists in large numbers. The adjective 多い comes at the end to complete the comment about quantity.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the focus changes to the store's action of selling many foreign goods.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate this as “there is” あります, but with 多い, the noun usually goes with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vi: It was cold last night, wasn't it?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with 夜, creating a noun phrase meaning “the night of yesterday.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes nighttime the topic of the comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 寒かった is the past form of the adjective 寒い, while ですね adds a sense of confirming the shared feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: きのうの modifies 夜 to identify a specific time. 夜は is the topic, and 寒かったですね expresses a feeling about the weather that occurred in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the sentence becomes a question about whether it was cold last night.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change 寒い into 寒かった when talking about past weather.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vi: I bought clothes at the department store.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the place where the buying action took place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks clothes as the object being bought.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the polite past form, showing that the buying action was completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: The place where the action takes place comes before the object, and they are marked in order by で and を. The verb 买う comes at the end and shows the main action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the sentence only says that the speaker went to the department store; it no longer means that they bought clothes.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the place where they buy something, but the place where the buying action takes place requires で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: I take medicine three times a day.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: A quantity phrase showing how often medicine is taken in one day.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks medicine as the object of the action of taking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 飲みます is the polite present form, expressing a habit or a regular instruction.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: 一日三回 places the frequency at the beginning of the sentence to limit how the action is performed. Medicine goes with を because it is the direct object of 飲みます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is added, the expression is still understandable, but it emphasizes one day as the unit for counting frequency.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for medicine, but something that is directly taken must go with を.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This part modifies 行きます and shows the way of moving.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction or destination of 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: The part showing the way comes before the place and the movement verb. The particle へ marks the direction of the action of going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: に also shows the destination and has almost the same meaning in this sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse へ with に, but へ emphasizes the direction of travel, while に emphasizes the destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents this room as the topic being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective ending in い comes before です to serve as a polite predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the quality used to describe it. An adjective ending in い keeps its original form before です.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: When it comes before a noun, the adjective directly modifies the room instead of serving as the predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: Do not add な after the adjective ending in い before です.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with 趣味, showing possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the hobby as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun comes before です to state the content of the hobby.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: The possessive phrase わたしの modifies 趣味. The pattern は + noun + です is used to identify what the hobby is.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence says that someone does the activity of cooking; it does not say that cooking is a hobby.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: の connects two nouns; を is not used in the phrase meaning “my hobby.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vi: I have a three-year-old son and a one-year-old daughter.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.sk: N は + Age の + N と + Age の + N が + います
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being talked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the age to 息子, showing the son's age.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects 息子 and 娘 in the same subject group.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the age to 娘, showing the daughter's age.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the group of people that exists together with わたし.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: います is used for the existence of people or animals.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: The age phrases come before the nouns and describe each child. と connects two nouns, while が marks the group of people as being present or existing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: や gives examples such as a son and a daughter, without necessarily listing everyone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: For people, use います, not あります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vi: The lesson is about to begin.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that something is about to happen.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the class as the subject that is about to begin.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb はじまる is in the polite form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.why: そろそろ comes before and describes the time when the action happens. With はじまる, the class is the subject, so use が, not を.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is still “about to begin,” but it focuses more on announcing an approaching time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with はじまる, but an event beginning usually goes with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Vました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces Amanda as the topic being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: A time word that adds information about the oversleeping.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ねぼうする is changed into the polite past form to describe an event that has already happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, followed by the time けさ and then the main action. けさ does not need a particle because it is used directly as a time adverb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning changes to “got up late,” describing the visible result rather than directly saying that the person overslept.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.tip: Do not translate ねぼうしました as only “got up late”; this word emphasizes sleeping past the proper time or oversleeping.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Vている
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes かない the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: いま indicates the present time of the state being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: でかける combines with ています to describe the state of currently being out.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.why: かないは is the topic, いま identifies the time, and でかけています is the predicate showing the current state. The ています form emphasizes the continuing state after going out.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this pattern only says that the wife is not in a certain place; it does not emphasize that she has gone out.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.tip: With でかけています, it does not necessarily mean that she is in the act of stepping outside; it usually means that she is currently out.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: お is a prefix that adds a polite and respectful tone when speaking about another person.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: じょうさん is a noun for a daughter or girl from another family.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.why: お comes before a noun to create a polite form of address. The whole phrase おじょうさん is used as a noun in the sentence, not as a complete sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: 娘さん also means someone else's daughter, but it is more ordinary in tone and does not contain the prefix おじょうさん.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use おじょうさん to refer to your own daughter when speaking formally about your family.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vi: If there is work left, I will do it after I get home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the work as what remains.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the past form modifies 場合 and creates the condition “if it remains.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 場合は states a hypothetical condition for the action in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of the action 帰る.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: てから connects two actions in order: the later action happens after the earlier one.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: します is the main action performed after returning home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, followed by the place and the order of actions. 場合は limits the situation, while てから identifies the action as happening after returning home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: ら expresses a condition more directly and naturally in conversation, while 場合は emphasizes a specific case.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Before 場合, use a modifying form such as Vた, not the polite form Vます directly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nの + 場合は; Vて + から
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vi: When taking medicine, drink plenty of water.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the medicine as the object being taken.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: とき comes after the dictionary form to create a time clause; は states that time as a condition requiring attention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks water as the object of the action in the main clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に changes 十分 into an adverb and modifies 飲んでください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: てください expresses a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: The time clause comes first to give the situation, followed by the main request. とき connects with the dictionary form because taking medicine is presented as a general time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the past form to mean that taking the medicine has already been completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: なら has the nuance “if you plan to take the medicine,” not simply a point in time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use です before とき; use the verb's modifying form, such as 飲むとき.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた + とき; Aい + とき; Aなな・Nの + とき; Vて + ください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: There is a large tree in the middle of the yard.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 庭 with 真ん中, creating the phrase “the middle of the yard.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the location where the tree exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before 木 to modify 木.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: あります describes the existence of an object.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: The location phrase 庭の真ん中に comes before the thing 木が, followed by あります to say that the thing exists there. The adjective 大きな comes directly before 木 to modify the tree.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で emphasizes the place where an action happens, so it does not fit a sentence that only describes existence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use で to show where an object exists; use に with あります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vi: The food will be served soon, so please wipe the table.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food being served.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being wiped.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects a verb with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to ask the listener to do something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.why: The 料理を出すので clause gives the reason first, followed by the request to wipe the table. The verb ふく changes to the て form to combine with ください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives the reason, but sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ふきましょう makes it an invitation to wipe the table together, rather than a request to the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(だ)・N(だ) ＋ ので; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vi: Last month, a baby was born. The baby's name is Haruka.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.sk: Time point、N が ＋ Vました。N は ＋ N です
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 先月 indicates when an event occurs and comes at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the baby as the subject of the birth event.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 生まれました is the polite past form and describes an event that has already happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes 名前 the topic of the following introduction.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: です connects the name はるか with 名前 to give an explanation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.why: The first sentence describes an event with 赤ちゃん as the subject. The second changes the topic to 名前 using は to provide information about the baby's name.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This way of speaking combines the two sentences into one and treats the baby's name as the subject being introduced.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish が, which states the subject of an event, from は, which changes to the topic to be explained.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vi: From now on, I intend to be in Japan in the future.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Time ＋ N に ＋ V辞書形 ＋ つもりです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person with the intention the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: これから indicates the starting point or a period extending toward the future.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 将来 adds the time when the intention will be carried out.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates where the subject いる exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern つもりです comes at the end of the sentence to express the speaker's intention or plan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.why: わたしは states the person with the intention, while the time phrases show the direction from the present to the future. 日本に comes before いる to indicate the place of existence, and つもりです turns the phrase いる into the content of the intention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 予定です makes the sentence focus more on an arranged plan or schedule than on a personal intention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ことにします emphasizes a decision that has been made, rather than simply stating an existing intention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put つもりです after a place noun, but a dictionary-form verb such as いるつもりです is needed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ つもりです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vi: Recently, I have been busy, so I have fewer chances to see my grandmother.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the recent time the topic of the comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 忙しい changes to 忙しくて to connect the reason to the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person whom the speaker meets.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 会う comes before 機会 to modify it and create the meaning “a chance to meet my grandmother.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks 機会 as the subject that is decreasing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: 減っています describes a state in which the number of chances has decreased and remains that way.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.why: 忙しくて connects the reason to the result in the main clause. The phrase 会う機会 is a modifying clause before the noun 機会, while 減っています is the main predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 忙しくて with 忙しいので still states the reason but separates the reason relationship more clearly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression emphasizes that the chances have become fewer. The meaning is similar, but it focuses on the result of “becoming fewer.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.tip: Do not put 会う after 機会; a verb modifying a noun must come before the noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.cn: Aいくて ＋ …; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vi: Youn is the tallest person in the class.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Range で ＋ 最も ＋ N が ＋ Aいです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Youn the person being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the range used to compare height.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 最も is an adverb that emphasizes the highest degree and modifies 高い.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks 背 as the aspect described by 高い.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 高いです is an adjective predicate that describes Youn's height.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.why: クラスで states the comparison group, while 最も comes before 高い to express the highest degree. In the pattern 背が高い, 背 is the aspect being evaluated, not the whole subject.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 最も with いちばん still means “the most,” but sounds more common and casual.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This also indicates the range “in the class” and makes the comparison slightly clearer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate 背が高い as “high back”; the whole phrase means “tall” or “tall in height.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vi: That person always wears a T-shirt.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states the person being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the item being worn.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The ている form describes an ongoing or maintained state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: The topic comes before は, and the adverb いつも then modifies the action of wearing. The object Tシャツ goes with を, while きています describes the continued state of wearing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern describes something made or placed in a certain state by someone. It is not used to say that a person is wearing something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as simply “doing,” but with the verb “wear,” it usually emphasizes the state of wearing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vi: Hotels stood in a row along the coast.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates the place and emphasizes the area along the coast.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject in the state of ならんでいた.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ていた describes an existing or ongoing state in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ いる／Vて形 ＋ いた when talking about a state or event in the past
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.why: The location phrase かいがんには sets the range first, and then ホテルが states what appears there. ならんでいた describes the hotels as being arranged in a row in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Using かいがんにホテルがあった only says that there are hotels there; it does not emphasize that they are arranged in a row.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 並んでいる changes the time of description to the present.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ていた as only “already,” but in this sentence it also describes the state of the hotels being arranged in a row.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q10.tokens.5.m: to line up / grow close together
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vi: A new apartment building is being built now.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: いま indicates the time when an action is in progress.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: あたらしい comes before a noun to modify マンション.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being built.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ている expresses an action that is continuing in the present.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.why: The time expression いま comes at the beginning of the sentence to show when the action happens. あたらしい modifies マンション, while を connects the object to the verb つくっています.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the polite form of Vている, and it still expresses an action in progress.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with つくりました, the building action will be understood as completed or as having happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out the particle を after マンション, but the object of つくる must be marked with を.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vi: At this time, the streets are quite empty.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.sk: Time expression は ＋ N が ＋ Vている
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents a time as the topic for comparison or comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that has the state すいています.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ている expresses that the streets are currently open and not crowded.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.why: The time expression このじかんは is made the topic. Then みちが is the subject of the state すいています. The form ています shows that the empty-street condition still exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If くるまがすくない is used, the sentence directly says that there are few vehicles instead of describing the street as empty.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If すいていました is used, the empty-street condition is placed at a time in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand すいている as “sparse,” but when it describes streets, it usually means empty or not crowded.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: The house key has been put in the desk drawer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 家 with かぎ to modify it and create the meaning “the house key.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は shows that the key is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の modifies drawer and creates the phrase “the desk drawer.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows where the object is placed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects the action of putting something with あります to express the resulting state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: あります shows that the key is already in a placed state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: The possessive phrases 家のかぎ and つくえのひきだし identify the key and its location. に marks the place, while 入れてあります shows that the object is in a state created by an intentional action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern only describes an existing state. It does not emphasize who put the key there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes putting something somewhere in advance to prepare for a later action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use に mechanically to indicate a place; for an object that has been placed in advance, it must be correctly combined with Vてあります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: What did that dish taste like?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the dish the topic being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: どんな comes before あじ to ask about the features or quality of the taste.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: でしたか creates a polite question about a past state or feature.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: 料理は is the topic, while どんなあじ asks about the dish's features. でしたか is used because the speaker is asking about the taste after tasting the dish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It can replace どんな in more formal speech, but the meaning of asking about the type or feature is similar.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: どんな must come before a noun; it cannot be placed directly after a noun as in the Vietnamese question “What is the taste like?”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vi: I live in the suburbs of Tokyo.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects Tokyo with こうがい to create the phrase “the suburbs of Tokyo.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates a fixed place of residence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 住んでいます expresses a state of living somewhere, not a temporary action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: 東京のこうがい creates a noun phrase referring to a place. The verb 住む goes with に because it describes a place of residence, and the form ています shows the current state of living there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で here is unnatural because 住む usually uses に to indicate a place of residence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that someone is going to or has gone to that place. It does not describe a long-term state of living there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: With 住む, remember to use に for a place of residence; で usually indicates the place where an action happens.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vi: It's hot, isn't it? Let's open the window a little.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.sk: Aい ですね。＋ 程度副詞 ＋ N を ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ ましょう
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: ですね is used to state a feeling and confirm it with the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the window as the object being opened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう attaches to the verb stem ます to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ ましょう
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence states the reason and creates agreement, while the second gives a suitable suggestion. 少し softens the action of opening the window, and を marks the object being opened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the invitation sounds more like a gentle request for an opinion, such as “Would you like to open it?”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern usually asks whether the speaker should do something for the listener. It is not simply a suggestion to do something together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.tip: ましょう is a suggestion to do something together, not a direct command to the listener alone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vi: I will make tea, so please boil some water for me.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks tea as what is being prepared.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause to the request in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the hot water as the object of boiling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the verb in the て form to ask the listener to do something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.why: The clause 入れるので gives the reason first, and then makes the request. わかしてください is the structure Vてください, in which boiling the water is requested politely.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational, and it may sometimes sound more subjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks for permission to do something, not for someone else to do it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; the verb before ください must change to the て form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なので／N＋なので; Vて形＋ください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vi: Getting around in this city is inconvenient.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the topic being commented on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that has the quality 不便.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends the polite sentence and connects with the adjective な 不便.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.why: The topic この町は is presented first. Then 交通が is the subject described by 不便です. The particle が identifies what is inconvenient.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning changes to say that there is little traffic, without emphasizing the inconvenience.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 交通, but the adjective 不便 uses が to identify the object that has that quality.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vi: The road is wet. It seems to have rained.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is in the state of ぬれている.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ている describes the road's current state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the event inferred in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ようだ follows the plain form to make an inference based on evidence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.why: The first sentence states the observable sign that the road is wet. Based on this sign, the second sentence uses ようだ after ふった to infer that it has rained.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 雨がふったそうだ is used, it means that the speaker heard someone say that it rained, rather than making an inference from the wet road.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: らしい also expresses an inference, but it is usually based more on known information or characteristics than on direct evidence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ようだ directly after a noun or adjective and forget the connecting forms のようだ and なようだ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + ようだ／Aな + なようだ／N + のようだ
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vi: Which floor is the toy counter on?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place whose location is being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: なんかい asks for the location by floor, while ですか makes the question polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.why: The place name is made the topic first. Then the question asks which floor that place is on. The pattern N は N ですか asks for the location or information about the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with どこですか, the question asks about the general location rather than specifically about the floor number.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand なんかい as asking about a number of times, but in a building context, なんかい means which floor.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vi: After coming home from school, please review the lesson.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から indicates the starting point of returning.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form た of a verb combines with ら to state a condition or the time after an action occurs.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects nouns and shows that the review content belongs to the lesson.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the content affected by してください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern てください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.why: The starting point is placed before the action of returning. Then, たら states when the return is completed, を marks what needs to be reviewed, and てください makes the request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてから is used, it emphasizes doing the second action after the first action is completed, with less of a conditional feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたあとで is used, it means after finishing the action. It is a neutral expression without the conditional feeling of たら.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that たら attaches to the past form た, not directly to the dictionary form of the verb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q1.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら; Vて + ください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vi: This pen is made in Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this pen is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 日本せい shows the place of production; です ends a noun sentence politely.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q10.kobun.why: The topic このペンは is placed first. Then 日本せいです serves as the predicate to state the product's origin. The particle は marks the object being introduced.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the pen was made in Japan in the passive form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q10.kobun.tip: Do not confuse せい in 日本せい with せいだ, which means a cause or a fault caused by someone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects これ with the noun that follows, giving the meaning of belonging to or being related to this.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes ざいりょう the topic being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: なんですか creates a polite question about the nature or name of the material.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.why: これの comes before ざいりょう to identify which object the material belongs to. なんですか comes at the end because it asks for the missing information about that topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the question asks what material or means was used to make this object.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually use は after これ by translating it as “this thing,” but here これの is what expresses the relationship “of this.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.cn: N の + N は + なんですか
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vi: I am interested in Japanese anime.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with アニメ, showing that the anime is related to Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that the speaker is interested in.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks きょうみ, the noun serving as the subject in the pattern きょうみがあります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: あります serves as the predicate and expresses that interest exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.why: 日本のアニメ forms a noun phrase, then に marks the field or object of interest. The pattern きょうみがあります uses が with きょうみ and あります as the predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence directly says “like Japanese anime,” with a simpler and stronger feeling of preference.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in this pattern as “at”; に only indicates the object or field toward which the interest is directed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.cn: N に + きょうみがある
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of a compound word meaning attendance or being present.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the last part, which combines with しゅっ to form a complete vocabulary word.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.why: The two parts combine to form one vocabulary unit, not a sentence with particles. This division helps learners compare the pronunciation of each part.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.tip: しゅっ should be pronounced with a small pause before せき, not as one long sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of a compound word related to producing a sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the last part, which combines with はつ to form a word meaning pronunciation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.why: The word is shown in two parts so learners can recognize how to read its components. When used in a sentence, はつおん is a noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.tip: Do not read おん as “ohn”; the sound おん needs a clearly pronounced final n.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of a compound word related to raising and training.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the last part, which combines with きょう to form a noun meaning education.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.why: The two parts form a compound vocabulary word, not a grammatical relationship like a complete sentence. Dividing it helps learners remember the pronunciation of each part.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.tip: Do not confuse きょういく with きょう, which means “today”; only the whole word きょういく means education.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: Even when I look at the map, I still do not understand. Let us ask at that police box over there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the map being looked at.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern ても connects to the following clause, meaning that even if the action is done, the result does not change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative verb describes the speaker's continuing state of not understanding.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The demonstrative あの modifies the noun こうばん that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle で indicates the place where the asking takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The form ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: を marks the map as the object being viewed, while ても creates a concessive relationship between looking at the map and not understanding the result. で identifies the place to ask, and ましょう makes a suggestion to do it together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If わかります is used instead, it means that we still understand even after looking, which is the opposite of the current result.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見たら is used, it means if or when we look at the map, without the meaning of still not understanding despite having looked.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate ても as “only after”; in this sentence, it means “even if... still...”.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.tokens.4.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.tokens.7.m: let us ask, let us ask together
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も; Vます-stem ＋ ましょう
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vi: My father founded a company when he was young and is still the director now.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は keeps my father as the topic throughout the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows when the father founded the company.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the company as the object that was founded.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the act of founding with the next clause in sequence and links the ideas.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: も emphasizes that the current state continues from before.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends a noun sentence and politely expresses the current position.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ following clause; N ＋ です
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: The topic, my father, is introduced at the beginning. Then, に identifies when he founded the company. The form て connects a past event with the current state, which is emphasized by も.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If つくって is replaced with つくったあとで, another action must happen after that, so it does not fit a direct connection to the current state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If まだ is used instead of 今も, it emphasizes that something has still not changed or ended. This has a different nuance from stating the current point in time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out も in 今も, which removes the meaning that the situation is still continuing as before.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: I have a sore throat. I may have caught a cold.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the body part that is painful.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いたい is the い adjective used as the predicate, showing a painful condition.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the action ひく.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ひいた is the past form of ひく, showing that the event may have happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: かもしれません is placed at the end of a sentence to show an uncertain guess.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: The first sentence uses が to state which body part hurts. The second sentence uses the past form of the verb before かもしれません to guess that catching a cold has already happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with でしょう, the sentence is still a guess, but it suggests stronger evidence or confidence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand かもしれません as a mild statement, but this pattern always keeps the meaning of uncertainty.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋かもしれません; N＋かもしれません
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vi: I played catch with my younger brother.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と shows the person who did the activity together with the speaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object that was thrown.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action なげる with the action あそぶ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The main verb is in the polite past form and ends the chain of actions.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.why: と identifies the person who took part, while を marks the ball. なげて comes before あそびました to connect the two actions in order or to treat throwing the ball as part of playing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ながら is used, the two actions are understood as happening at the same time, without emphasizing their order.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the person doing something together with you. For the meaning “together with someone,” use と.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; Vて ＋ ください; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vi: My country exports a lot of rice abroad.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: わたしの modifies 国 and shows possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes my country the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the direction or destination of the export.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the goods being exported.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: おおく modifies the action of exporting and shows the amount of rice.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects the verb ゆしゅつする with いる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: いる follows the て form to show that the export is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.why: The sentence states the topic first with は, then places the destination with に and the goods with を. ゆしゅつしている describes an export activity that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If the dictionary form is used, the sentence only describes exporting in general and does not emphasize continuation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out いる after the て form, causing the sentence to lose the nuance that the action is “continuing or still being maintained.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vi: I lost yesterday’s tennis match. Next time, I want to win.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase stands at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the match took place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: テニスの modifies しあい and forms the phrase “tennis match.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the situation or competition in which the loss happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: まけました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: は introduces next time as a new topic and contrasts it with the time the speaker lost.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: たいです is attached to the verb stem to show the speaker’s wish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.why: で places the loss in the context of the match, while は in the next sentence shifts the topic to next time to create a contrast. たいです expresses the speaker’s wish about a future action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つもりです, the sentence focuses more on a firm intention or plan than on a wish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.tip: たいです usually means “want,” and does not necessarily carry the meaning of being required to do something, as “must” does.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ たいです; Vます-stem ＋ たくないです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vi: This city has long been famous for soccer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time から ＋ N が ＋ Aなです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents this city as the topic being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point of the state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject described as active or popular.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: さかんです is the な adjective predicate describing the state of soccer activity.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.why: は defines the scope of the comment as this city, while が marks the field being described. から shows that the active state of soccer began at a point in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with にぎやかです, the meaning is that the city in general is lively, not specifically that soccer is active.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.tip: から in this sentence means “since” or “from,” not “because,” which shows a cause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vi: Sakura has become a little thinner.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents Sakura as the person being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: すこし modifies やせました and shows the degree of change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: やせました is the polite past form of the verb, showing a change in body shape.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.why: は makes Sakura the topic, while すこし comes before the predicate to limit the degree of change. やせる itself expresses the process of becoming thinner, so no extra change verb is needed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 細[ほそ]くなりました, the sentence emphasizes that the body has become slimmer or smaller, which is not exactly the same as becoming thinner.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use すこし as an independent noun. This word usually comes before a verb or adjective to show degree.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t14-q9.tokens.1.m: older sister; you (polite form of address)
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vi: I received a letter from my friends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: からの modifies てがみ and shows that the letter came from my friends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the letter as the thing received.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: うけとりました is a polite past-tense verb that describes receiving and accepting an item.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.why: からの combines with the noun that follows to form the phrase “a letter from my friends.” This phrase is the object with を, and the past-tense verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: もらいました emphasizes that the speaker received the letter as something sent to them, while うけとりました emphasizes the act of receiving.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use から alone before a verb, but here からの must connect directly to the noun てがみ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vi: I asked Takashi how to use a computer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.sk: Person に + N の + N を + Vました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person being asked in the action たずねました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects パソコン with つかいかた to indicate how to use the computer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content that the speaker wants to ask about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: たずねました is a polite past-tense predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while the content of the question goes with を. の turns パソコン into a modifier for つかいかた, forming “how to use the computer.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: 聞きました can mean either ask or listen, so its meaning is wider than たずねました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily switch the two particles and use を for the person being asked instead of for the content of the question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.sk: Person に + N を + Vました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the thanks.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks おれい as the content that is said.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: いいました is a polite past-tense predicate that means the speaker said thanks.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.why: The listener or receiver of the words goes with に, while the content being said goes with を. The verb いいました comes at the end of the sentence and takes the past tense to show that the thanks were said.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression gives the exact words of thanks, so it is more specific than おれいをいいました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily omit に before the receiver or use と when the sentence only generally expresses “say thanks.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.why: This is an independent vocabulary item, not a complete sentence, so it has no subject, object, or predicate relationship within a sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.tip: Do not confuse しょうたい with しょうち because the two words sound similar but have different meanings.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vi: That is dangerous. Please watch out for cars.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: です forms a polite predicate, while よ emphasizes the warning for the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that needs attention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of ちゅういする, and it connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.why: 車にちゅういする uses に to mark the object that needs attention. The verb て combines with ください to make a polite reminder or request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This structure is also a reminder to be careful with cars, but it uses 気をつける with a tone of paying attention to avoid danger.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use ちゅういをしてください, but the natural expression here is ちゅういしてください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: I went to a concert and listened to music.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or event that the speaker goes to.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 行って is the て form of 行く, connecting the action of going with the action of listening to music.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks music as the object being listened to.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the polite past form, placed at the end to show the result of the sequence of actions.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.why: に attaches to the destination of 行く. 行って connects the two actions in order, while 聞きました at the end gives the whole sentence a past tense.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, it means listening to music at the concert venue, emphasizing where the action takes place rather than the destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use で with 行く, but verbs that show movement toward a destination usually use に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vi: This is an important document to submit when enrolling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the thing being presented or explained.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects にゅうがく with とき to form the phrase “the time of enrollment.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time when the document must be submitted.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause 出す comes before しょるい and modifies the document being submitted.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: たいせつな is an な adjective that directly modifies しょるい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the noun sentence and confirms that this is an important document.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.why: The phrase にゅうがくのときに indicates the time, while 出す comes before しょるい to specify which document. たいせつな continues to modify the same noun before the sentence ends with です.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出した is used, it means a document that has been submitted, rather than a document that needs to be submitted.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily place 出す after しょるい, but a modifying clause in Japanese always comes before the noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Aな + な + N; N + の + N
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the language being translated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the target language of the translation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ほんやくします is a polite verb that comes at the end of the sentence to state the main action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.why: The source language goes with を, while the target language goes with に. The verb ほんやくします comes at the end of the sentence after these two necessary parts.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, 日本語から shows that the source language is Japanese, changing the direction of the translation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.tip: English speakers may confuse を and に, but English is the content being translated, so it goes with を, while Japanese is the destination, so it goes with に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vi: Every year, my family gathers during the New Year holiday.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.sk: N time + N は + N が + Vます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates repeated time and is placed at the beginning of the sentence to give the context.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: as for the New Year holiday
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes しょうがつ the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that performs the gathering action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: あつまります is a polite predicate that describes the family gathering.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.why: 毎年 gives the general frequency, while しょうがつは limits the topic to the New Year holiday. The family is the subject, so が is used, and あつまります ends the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, しょうがつに only indicates the time when the family gathers; it does not create a topic-setting meaning like は.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.tip: English speakers may translate は and が in the same way, but here は introduces the topic, while が marks the subject of the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vi: Tomorrow is the university entrance ceremony. From now on, I will attend university for four years.
