default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.sk: N は + N の + N です。 + Time point + Time period + N に + Vます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 大学 to the noun that follows and modifies that noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and expresses a polite statement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: これから indicates the time when an action begins.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: This time expression comes before the verb and shows the length of study.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the destination of the action 通います.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: 通います is the main predicate. It uses the polite present form to describe an action that will continue.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.why: The first sentence uses は to state tomorrow, then uses の to connect 大学 with the event name. The second sentence places the starting point, duration, destination, and finally the main verb 通います.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: へ also indicates the direction toward the university, but it emphasizes direction more than に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に before a place and say 大学通います directly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学校 with 規則, meaning that the rules belong to the school.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the rules as the object that must be followed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: てください follows the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.why: The phrase 学校のきそく forms a compound noun. Then を marks the object of the verb. The てください form comes at the end to turn the action into a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also asks someone to do something, but it has a stronger command-like tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put を in the wrong position and place it after 学校 instead of after the noun for the rules.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vi: I will tell Mr. Tanaka the meeting time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.sk: N の + N を + Person に + Vます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かいぎ with 時間 to indicate the time belonging to the meeting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the meeting time as the information being reported.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person receiving the information.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: しらせます is the predicate and describes giving information to the recipient.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.why: The information being reported comes first and takes を, while the recipient takes に. This order makes the content clear before stating who receives it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 伝えます also means conveying something to Tanaka, but it emphasizes passing words or content to that person.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に and を, using に for the information being reported instead of for the recipient.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vi: Although I practiced yesterday, I forgot the kanji.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vた ＋ のに ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ しまいました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates the time when the practice took place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects an event that happened with an unexpected result in the next clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 漢字 as the object of the verb わすれる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb わすれる with しまいました to create a pattern expressing an accidental or regrettable action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました shows that the action has been completed, often with a sense of regret or unwillingness.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.why: きのう states the time. Then のに connects the completed practice with the unexpected result of forgetting the kanji. 漢字を is the object of わすれる, while Vてしまう emphasizes the regrettable result.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with けれども, the sentence still means “but,” but the sense of regret and unexpectedness is weaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If only 忘れました is used, the sentence only states that the speaker forgot something and does not emphasize regret or unwillingness.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit しまう because they translate 忘れてしまいました simply as “forgot,” losing the sense of regret.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being asked.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action of drinking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: めしあがります is the honorific predicate, while か turns the sentence into a polite question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.why: The person being asked comes before は, the thing being consumed comes before を, and the verb comes at the end. The honorific form of the verb is suitable when talking about an action performed by someone who should be respected.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it gives another polite question, but uses the regular honorific pattern of 飲む.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain form of the verb when you want to keep a polite questioning tone with a superior.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vi: After hearing the news, I was very surprised.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the content that was heard.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of listening with the result that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and expresses the result or feeling after the previous action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.why: ニュースをを marks what was heard. The て form connects the action of listening with the surprised reaction, and the final verb states the main event.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with てから, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker became surprised only after finishing listening.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.tip: Do not translate て as an independent action. Here, it connects the previous cause or process with the later result.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vi: Have you decided which store to choose yet?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は brings the topic of choosing a store forward for the question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies the verb and shows that the action being asked about may already be complete.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: きめました is a polite past-tense verb that combines with か to ask whether an action has been completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.why: The topic comes before は. もう indicates the present time with the meaning “already,” while the past-tense verb in the question checks whether the decision has been completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the question shifts toward whether the listener may still have not decided.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.tip: もう with Vましたか usually asks “have you done it yet?” It should not simply be understood as “do it one more time.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: おじゃま is a noun for disturbing someone and is the object of します.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: します completes the polite greeting おじゃまします when entering someone else’s home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.why: The noun おじゃま combines with します to create a polite expression used when the speaker is about to enter or is inside someone else’s home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is also a polite request for permission, but it has the broader meaning “excuse my rudeness.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.tip: Do not translate おじゃまします as a serious act of disturbing someone. It is a social greeting used when entering another person’s home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vi: To look at, read, or look through something humbly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: はいけん is an action noun in the humble compound word 拝見する.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: する combines with an action noun to create the humble verb “look.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.why: はいけん belongs to a group of nouns that can combine with する to form verbs. The whole phrase uses humble language for the speaker’s action of looking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見る is used, the sentence only has the ordinary form and does not show humility.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.tip: This humble form is used for the speaker’s own action, not to show respect for another person’s action of looking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks コップ as the object that is in a broken state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: われています uses the ている form to describe the present state after the cup has broken.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.why: コップが is the thing that has the state, while われています describes the present state caused by the previous action of breaking. Therefore, が is more suitable than を in this sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If われました is used, the sentence focuses on the event of the cup breaking and does not emphasize its present state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If こわされています is used, the meaning changes to the cup being damaged or smashed by someone, showing another person’s action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate and use the ている form as the present continuous tense, but here it only indicates the state “has broken and is still broken.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vi: Speaking in front of everyone makes me nervous.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects みんな with 前, forming the phrase “in front of everyone”.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place or situation where the speaking action takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 話すの changes a verb into a noun referring to an action, while は makes that action the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: きんちょうします is the predicate and describes a tense or nervous state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.why: みんなの前で states the situation of the speaking action. 話すのは makes “speaking” the topic, and then きんちょうします states the feeling caused by that action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is replaced with 話すと, the sentence means “whenever one speaks in front of everyone, …,” emphasizing a condition or a natural result.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 話すことは is used, the expression about speaking in front of everyone sounds more general or formal.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget の when they want to turn the verb 話す into a noun placed before は.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vi: A: One coffee, please. B: Yes, certainly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the thing being requested.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 一つ indicates the quantity of the requested item.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ください is placed at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: はい is a confirming reply to the previous statement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: かしこまりました is a very polite reply when accepting a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.why: The requested item goes with を, and the quantity is then placed before ください. The reply はい comes first, while かしこまりました ends the polite confirmation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the request remains polite but has a more general asking-for-help tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often place 一つ after ください, but the quantity usually comes before ください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vi: A: Do you have children? B: Yes, I have one child.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は introduces お子さん as the topic being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: いらっしゃいますか forms a polite question about the existence of a person.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: はい confirms the previous question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 一人 indicates the number of children and adds information about おります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: おります is the humble form of います, used for the existence of someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.why: お子さんは makes the person being asked about the topic, and then いらっしゃいますか asks respectfully about their existence. The answer gives the quantity first and then uses おります to speak humbly about the speaker’s side.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If います is used, the basic meaning does not change, but the level of politeness and respect is lower.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use あります for people, but for people they should use います or a polite form such as いらっしゃいます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vi: If you read a book on a boat, you will feel sick.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で indicates the place where the reading action takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the thing being read.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 読 corresponds to と and connects a condition with a natural result that follows the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle が marks the subject that enters an unwell state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: わるくなります shows a change into a worse state; よ emphasizes the information as a reminder.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.why: 船で identifies where the action happens, and 本を is the object of 読む. Clause 読むと states the preceding condition, while 気持ちがわるくなります is the natural result.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used instead, the sentence expresses a more specific hypothetical condition rather than a usual result.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に for the place where they read, but the location where an action takes place uses で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vi: I bumped into a bicycle and got injured.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle と indicates the object of the collision.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the collision with the result that happens afterward.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks けが as something the speaker experienced.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.why: 自転車と identifies the object of the collision, and the て form connects that event with the result of being injured. けがをしました describes the injury as an event that has already happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the cause-and-effect relationship is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with ぶつかる, but the object of a collision usually goes with と.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vi: A: I have had a fever since yesterday. B: I see. Get well soon.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.sk: Time point から + N が あります。 + 応答 + おだいじに
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle から indicates the starting point of the fever.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: あります describes an ongoing state, here having a high temperature or fever symptoms.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: そうですか is a reply that accepts the information just heard.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: おだいじに is a wish used at the end of a sentence when the listener is ill.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.why: きのうから places the starting point before 熱があります to state when the symptom began. After receiving the information with そうですか, the listener ends with a caring expression suitable for the illness.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus is on a fever that is occurring or rising.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate から as “because,” but in this sentence から indicates a starting point in time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vi: I will come to your place tomorrow.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.sk: Time point + N へ + humble V
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle へ indicates the destination of the movement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: まいります is the humble form of いきます or きます, used to speak politely about the speaker’s movement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.why: あした places the time at the beginning of the sentence, followed by そちらへ, which states the destination. The subject is omitted because it is clear from the context, while まいります comes at the end as the predicate and shows humility.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is still going there, but the expression is more ordinary and does not show humility.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand まいります as only “go,” but this word can also mean “come,” depending on the viewpoint in the context.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vi: I intend to give this doll to Sakura.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the item being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the receiver of the gift.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb あげる comes before つもりです to express the speaker’s intention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.why: は places the topic at the beginning of the sentence, に marks the receiver, and あげるつもりです forms the predicate phrase showing intention. The verb before つもり must be in the dictionary form when talking about an intention to do something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 予定です makes the sentence focus more on a planned schedule and less on personal intention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に as the direct object; with あげる, the gift uses を, while the receiver uses に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Nの ＋ つもりだ
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vi: I will send an email when I finish the work.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the work that must be completed in the conditional clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a condition or an earlier time with the following action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: メールします is an action planned after the work is finished.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.why: ようじがすんだら creates a time or condition point, and then the action メールします follows. The subjects of the two clauses can be understood as the same person, so they do not need to be repeated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with すんだあとで, the sentence simply states the time order and has less of a conditional feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use the dictionary form before たら, but they must use the past form た of the verb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vi: I have an important task that day.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents that day as the time point being mentioned.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: あります describes the existence of the task.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.why: The day is made the topic with は, while the task is the thing that exists, so it goes with が. The adjective だいじな comes before the noun しごと to modify it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たいせつな, the basic meaning is still important, but the nuance may focus more on respect or value.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with あります, but a thing that exists must go with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vi: Yesterday's movie was not interesting at all.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a time noun with the noun えいが to modify it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the movie as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ちっとも emphasizes a zero degree and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: おもしろくありませんでした is the past negative form of the adjective ending in い.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.why: きのうのえいが creates a noun phrase, and then は makes the movie the topic. ちっとも comes before the negative predicate to emphasize that the movie was not interesting at all.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ぜんぜん～ない, the negative meaning remains clear, but the tone is more neutral and does not emphasize the idea of not even a little.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with あまり～ない, the negative degree is weaker and only means that it was not very interesting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use ちっとも with an affirmative sentence, but this pattern must be combined with a negative form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.cn: ちっとも ＋ Vない・Aいくない・Aなではない・Nではない
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vi: I added miso to the soup. As a result, it became very tasty.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the thing that something is added to.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks miso as the thing that was added.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 足しました is the polite past form of 足す and acts as the predicate for an action that happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すると connects the earlier action with the result that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the adjective おいしい to show degree.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the form おいしく to connect with なる and express a change of state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました describes a new state that has formed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.why: The first sentence states the action of adding miso, and the second uses すると to give the result. おいしく comes before なりました because the adjective must change to a linking form when expressing a change with なる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using おいしくしました means that someone actively makes the soup tasty, instead of the soup becoming tasty by itself.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily keep おいしい before なる; it must be changed to おいしくなる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vi: When the season changes from autumn to winter, it gets dark earlier.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the season as the subject that changes.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of the change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of the change, and と emphasizes the change to a new state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 変わり is the linking form of 変わる and connects the seasonal change with the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject of the phenomenon 暮れる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: の turns the clause 暮れる into a noun, and が marks it as the subject of 早くなった.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: 早くなった describes the time when it gets dark changing to an earlier time than before.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: から and へと indicate the starting point and destination of the change, respectively. The clause 暮れるのが is turned into a noun to serve as the subject of 早くなった.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 早くした means that a person or agent makes it get dark earlier, so it is no longer a natural change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily leave out の in 暮れるのが; の is necessary to turn the whole clause into a noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: I hear that a new supermarket will open nearby soon.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where something appears or is built.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 新しい comes before スーパー to modify that noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the supermarket as the object that newly appears.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: できる in the dictionary form comes before そうです to report information that was heard.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.why: The place comes before the subject in the pattern Nに Nができる, meaning that a new building or facility appears somewhere. そうです at the end of the sentence shows that this is reported information.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: できそうです means that something seems possible to make or seems nearly complete, based on the speaker's judgment rather than reported information.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may understand できる here as “can”; in the pattern NにNができる, it usually means that something is built or opened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vi: It rained very heavily yesterday, so we could not play soccer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes yesterday the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks rain as the phenomenon being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ひどくて is the linking form of the adjective ひどい and connects the cause with the result in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks playing soccer as the activity that could not be done.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: できませんでした describes something that could not be done in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.cn: Aい → Aいくて、＋ result clause
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.why: きのうは identifies the time, and ひどくて connects the cause of heavy rain with the result of being unable to play soccer. With the ability form できる, activities that can or cannot be done usually go with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ひどいので still states the cause, but the explanatory tone is more direct and clear.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ひどかったので emphasizes that the rain was heavy in the past as a completed cause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily connect the cause with から after ひどい; if they use the form て, they must change ひどい to ひどくて.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vi: I practice a lot, but I still cannot improve.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects the previous clause with an opposite idea in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: なかなか is often used with a negative sentence to describe something that is difficult to happen or has still not been achieved.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: うまく is an adverb form that modifies なります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: なりません is the polite negative form of なります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.why: The first clause says that the person practices a lot, and then が changes to an opposite result. なかなか combines with the negative form to stress that improvement has still not been achieved.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning becomes stronger and emphasizes that the person does not improve at all.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that なかなか in this meaning usually has to be used with a negative sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vi: This road is crowded, so let us take another road.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this road the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the route or means used for traveling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the topic and condition of the road, then uses から to give the reason. The phrase 別の道で comes before 行きましょう and indicates the chosen route.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective, while the suggestion remains unchanged.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of で when saying that they travel by or along a road.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vi: I prepared a present for my friends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the receiver of the present.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that was prepared.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: よういしました is the predicate and describes a completed preparation action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.why: The receiver goes with に, the prepared item goes with を, and the verb comes at the end of the sentence. This order clearly shows who receives what.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ともだちのために, the meaning emphasizes preparing something for the benefit of the friends rather than directly for the friends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily reverse に and を or use を for the receiver.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the coat should be placed or hung.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 上着 as the item affected by the hanging action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb form て＋ください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.why: The place ここに comes before the object and action to show where the action should take place. 上着を is the object, while かけてください ends the sentence with a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a question or permission to hang the coat.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place に after the object, but in this pattern the place に comes before Nを.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vi: My younger brother is shorter than me.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes my younger brother the subject of comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the standard used for comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the feature being evaluated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ひくい is the い adjective used as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.why: より places the standard of comparison before the feature being compared. The pattern NはNよりNがAい describes an attribute of the subject as higher or lower than the standard.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If the noun showing the attribute and が are omitted, the sentence can still be understood as a comparison, but the meaning is less clear in this sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the order and directly connect the subject with the adjective, forgetting より to show the standard of comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vi: Please tell me the reason you were late.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time used as a standard and combines with おくれる to show being late.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: A past-tense clause comes before the noun to modify 理由.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the reason as the content that is requested to be spoken about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 話してください is a polite way to make a request, in which てください connects to the verb to request an action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.why: The clause おくれた comes directly before the noun to limit the type of reason being discussed. That noun is the object of 話してください, so it goes with を.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used after 理由, the reason becomes the topic for explanation instead of the content that is requested to be spoken about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, while Japanese places it before the noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vi: I thought very carefully, but I still did not understand.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies the action of thinking and shows the degree to which it was performed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: けど connects two clauses with opposite meanings: the person thought carefully, but still did not understand.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ませんでした is the polite past negative form and describes a result that did not happen.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.why: よく comes before the verb to add the degree of the action. けど comes after the first clause to connect it with the unexpected result in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If けど is replaced with が, the contrast remains, but the tone becomes more formal and written.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence emphasizes that the result is contrary to expectations or feels more regrettable.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate けど as an independent linking word and forget that it must be attached directly after the first clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ ＋ けど
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vi: Because it is cold, my ears feel freezing cold.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い changes into the form くて to connect the reason or state with the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part with the described state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: つめたいです is the polite predicate describing the state of the ears.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.why: さむくて connects the cold state with the result that follows. The subject of the following state is みみ, so が is used, and the adjective つめたい serves as the predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of くて, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer and the sentence sounds more politely explanatory.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If し is used, the idea of being cold sounds like one reason listed together with other reasons.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep さむい unchanged and connect it directly, but the adjective い must change into さむくて.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vi: The exam will start at one o'clock.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time から ＋ Nする
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the exam the topic of information about its starting time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the time when an event starts.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 開始します is the verb predicate サ変. It uses the noun 開始 together with します to describe the action of starting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.why: しけん is made the topic with は. １時から identifies the starting point in time, while 開始します serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence only states a specific starting time and does not emphasize starting from that point.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 始まります is used, the beginning is expressed with an intransitive verb instead of the noun 開始 combined with します.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers easily use に by habit with all time points, but から is needed when saying “from the starting time.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vi: I like meat more than fish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose preference is being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the food used as the standard for comparing preferences.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: のほうが marks the side that is chosen or valued more highly in the comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きです is the predicate expressing preference, with the liked object as the subject with が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.why: 魚より states the food used as the standard, while にくのほうが states the side valued more highly. These two parts combine before 好きです to form a comparison of preferences.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a question asking which food is preferred.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with も, the sentence only says that the speaker also likes meat and no longer means that meat is preferred to fish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out のほうが because they think より is enough, but のほうが is needed to mark the chosen side as better.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.cn: N より ＋ N のほうが
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vi: I always keep my wallet, phone, and other important things in my bag.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle や connects nouns given as examples.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: など shows that these are examples from a wider group.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the group of objects being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates where the objects are put.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb in the ている form expresses the habit of keeping things stored.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.why: や and など create an open list, and then は groups all the objects as the topic. The phrase かばんに indicates where the objects are kept, while いれている expresses a current habit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used instead of や, the sentence gives a complete list limited to the wallet and phone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入れてある is used, the sentence emphasizes that the objects have been placed there by someone, rather than the speaker’s habit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse や with と; や usually means “and other things,” not a complete list.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vi: When I finish my work, I will tidy up the top of my desk.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that finishes the action in the conditional clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form おわった combines with ら to create a condition or the time “when...”.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects じぶん with the noun つくえ to show possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects つくえ with 上, creating the phrase “the top of the desk.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the part being tidied.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.why: The clause おわったら places the time condition before the main action. The sequence じぶんのつくえの上 modifies the noun phrase layer by layer and identifies exactly what is being tidied.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence focuses on a result that naturally or inevitably happens as soon as the work ends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If あとで is used, the sentence only says “after finishing” and does not have as clear a conditional meaning as たら.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out の in the possessive sequence, causing the phrases “my desk” and “the top of the desk” to lose their linking relationship.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vi: I was very happy because I received flowers on my birthday.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the flowers were received.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects receiving the flowers with the feeling of happiness in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the past form to describe a feeling that happened in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.why: に places the event on the birthday, while を marks the flowers as the thing received. The て form connects the cause or event leading to the happy feeling at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらったので is used, the cause “because I received it” is stated more clearly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If もらったとき is used, the sentence only emphasizes the time when the flowers were received, not the connection leading to the feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate て as a fixed “and,” but here it connects an event that causes the feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vi: Lee is wearing a red hat.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states Lee as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 赤い comes before ぼうし to modify the hat; を marks the hat as the thing being worn.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: かぶる is divided into かぶっている to express the state of wearing a hat.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.why: Lee is the topic at the beginning of the sentence. The phrase 赤いぼうし comes before を as the object. 赤い directly modifies ぼうし, while かぶっています expresses the state of wearing it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 赤くて is used, 赤い connects to another clause or quality and no longer directly modifies ぼうし.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 赤い after the noun, but the い-ending adjective must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose ability to attend is being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects きょう with かいぎ to create the phrase “today’s meeting.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the event that the speaker attends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: できません is a polite negative form expressing a lack of ability or the conditions needed to attend.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.why: は identifies the speaker, の creates the noun phrase “today’s meeting,” and に marks the event being attended. できません comes at the end to state the ability that is negated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If しません is used, the sentence means “will not attend,” expressing only a decision or action, not necessarily inability.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also expresses inability to attend, but it is a more informal negative form than できません.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with しゅっせき, but this noun usually goes with に to indicate a meeting or event that someone attends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vi: My older sister and I have very similar faces.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects わたし with あね to form the group of people being compared.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the group “my older sister and I” as the topic of comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the body part that has the shared feature.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: にている describes a similar state between two people or things.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.why: と joins the two people as the object of comparison, while は covers the whole group as the topic. かおが is the subject with the similar feature, and にている describes the similar state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If そっくりです is used, the meaning is stronger, emphasizing that the two faces are almost identical.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 同じです is used, the sentence may mean completely identical or similar in one specific feature.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use とても to connect two people; と is the particle connecting the objects, while とても indicates the degree “very.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vi: When I talk with people I meet for the first time, I feel nervous.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause modifies 人, meaning a person whom one meets for the first time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the person one talks with.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: とき indicates a time, while は presents the situation as the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.why: The clause はじめてあう modifies 人, forming the phrase “a person one meets for the first time.” The phrase はなすときは gives the time and situation, and then どきどきする serves as the main predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 会った is used, it means a person one met for the first time and emphasizes that the event has happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often forget は after とき when they want to make the whole situation the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vi: I made this cake. Please enjoy it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: このケーキ is the topic placed first and separated by a comma.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who made the cake.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: どうぞ adds the meaning of inviting or encouraging the listener to do the next action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: てください creates a polite request; めしあがる is the respectful form of 食べる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.why: The noun このケーキ is presented as the topic, while わたしが identifies the person who performs the action つくりました. After the statement, どうぞ introduces an invitation using the Vてください pattern.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べてください, the sentence is still an invitation to eat, but the tone is ordinary and does not show respect for the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the kanji spelling of めしあがってください, so the meaning and tone do not change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use 食べてください with everyone and forget to use respectful language when inviting a guest.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vi: A: What is the relationship between Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Kimura? B: Those two are brothers.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two nouns whose relationship is being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes Tanaka and Kimura the topic of the question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: どういう modifies かんけい and asks about the type or content of the relationship.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ですか creates a polite question about the noun かんけい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: は presents the two people just mentioned as the topic of the answer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the sentence with a noun, while よ emphasizes the information given to the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.why: The question uses どういう to modify かんけい, creating the structure “what kind of relationship.” The answer changes the topic to あのふたり and uses the noun きょうだい as the predicate with よ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If どんな関係 is used, the question asks about the type of relationship in a similar way, but sounds more conversational.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 何の関係 is used, the question focuses more directly on “what relationship do they have with each other?”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often confuse どういう with どうして; どういう asks about the content or type, while どうして asks about the reason.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vi: A: It is great that you came. Please come in. B: Excuse me for coming in.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: よく combines with いらっしゃいました to form a greeting that welcomes a guest.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: いらっしゃいました is the respectful form of 来ました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: どうぞ is a short invitation that allows the guest to enter or use what is being offered naturally.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: おじゃまします is a fixed greeting used when entering someone’s home or disturbing someone else’s space.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.why: いらっしゃいました describes the guest’s arrival using respectful language. After the invitation どうぞ, the guest replies with おじゃまします as a polite announcement when entering the house.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 失礼します, it means “excuse me for being rude” and is used more broadly when entering, leaving, or interrupting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 入ります, it only describes the action of entering and loses the polite greeting meaning.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate おじゃまします as “disturb” in a negative sense, but it is mainly a fixed social expression.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q26.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents ねだん as the topic being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q26.kobun.ch.1.n: わかりますか asks whether the listener knows the information about the price.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q26.kobun.why: ねだん is made the topic by は, and then わかりますか asks whether the listener understands the information. This structure focuses on understanding or knowing the information, not directly on asking for the number.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q26.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いくらですか, the question directly asks how much the price is.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q26.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 知っていますか, the question focuses on whether the information is already known.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q26.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use わかりますか to ask for a specific amount of money, while いくらですか directly asks “how much does it cost?”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the type of tea being described; the comma separates the topic from the description.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks a feeling or feature that is perceived.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.ch.2.n: する combines with あじ to describe what kind of taste the tea has.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.why: このおちゃは makes the object the topic, while へんなあじがする uses する to describe the taste sensation produced by the tea. The adjective へんな comes before the noun あじ to modify “taste.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with おかしなあじがする, it still means that the tea has a strange taste, but sounds more conversational and slightly stranger.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with あじがおかしい, the sentence emphasizes that the taste is abnormal rather than the feeling of “having a strange taste.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q27.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often say あじをする, but taste sensations use がする.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.vi: Next week, I will go to meet my teacher.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行きます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates the time when the action happens.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the person whom the speaker is going to meet.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.ch.2.n: The ます form of あいます combines with に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行きます describes the main action, which is going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the person one is going to meet. The pattern Vます remove ます＋に＋行く expresses the purpose of going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.vs.0.d: If this verb is used instead, the sentence focuses more on visiting or calling on someone, not on the action of meeting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q28.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often forget に after the ます form when expressing the purpose of going to do something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.vi: This is the first time I have made a mistake like this.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.ch.0.n: こんな modifies the noun ミス that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes making this kind of mistake the topic of the comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.ch.2.n: はじめてです serves as the predicate and states that this is a first-time experience.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.why: こんな comes before the noun to limit the type of mistake being discussed. Nは はじめてです creates a structure stating that this experience is happening for the first time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the tone is more formal and refers to a type of mistake that has already been mentioned or is already known.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q29.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often place こんな after the noun, but this pattern must come before the noun to modify it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Frequency + N を + Vている
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks Tanaka as the person being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.ch.1.n: This part indicates the time when the action usually takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.ch.2.n: This word modifies the action that follows. It indicates a high frequency, but not without exception.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks work as the object of the action of doing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.ch.4.n: している is the ている form of する. It expresses a state or an action that continues.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time and frequency, and then the object of the action. している comes at the end as the main predicate and shows that the activity is continuing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used instead, the meaning becomes “work almost always,” or, depending on a negative sentence, “hardly work at all.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q30.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate たいてい as “always,” but this word still allows for exceptions.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q31.kobun.why: This is a compound noun pronounced as きょうみ. It is usually used to talk about interest or concern.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q31.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern expresses having an interest in or concern for an object.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q31.kobun.vs.1.d: This word has a similar meaning, but it usually carries a stronger sense of serious attention or concern.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q31.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily misread きょうみ as a word with the sound きょみ or incorrectly lengthen the sound きょう.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q32.tokens.0.m: recover from an illness, be repaired
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.vi: Yes, I understand and will do it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.sk: fixed expression かしこまりました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the fixed polite expression かしこまりました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.ch.1.n: ました gives the reply a past and polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.why: かしこまりました is a polite reply when accepting another person’s request or instructions. ました gives the sentence a polite tone and shows that the request has been accepted.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.vs.0.d: If わかりました is used instead, the sentence still means “understood,” but it is less formal and has a weaker service-related tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q34.kobun.tip: Do not use かしこまりました in every informal situation; it is an especially polite expression.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vi: This is the district’s art museum.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the topic being introduced.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 区 with 美術館 and shows a possessive relationship.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: です creates a polite noun predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the topic これは, then uses 区の to modify 美術館. The pattern Nです identifies the subject as a particular noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning emphasizes that the museum is located in that district, and does not necessarily belong to the district.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の as “at” or “in,” but in this sentence の shows a relationship of “belonging to” or possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vi: I am researching flowers at the university.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person carrying out the research.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the research takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being studied.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the ている form of 研究する. It describes an activity that is being carried out or continuing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.why: The place of the activity comes before the object and predicate: 大学で → 花を → 研究しています. The particle で indicates where the action takes place, while を indicates the object of 研究する.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means that the research was completed in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the place where an activity is taking place; for actions such as researching, studying, and working, use で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 彼 the topic being introduced.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects わたし with 主人 and shows a possessive or marital relationship.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun 主人 combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.why: 彼は is the topic, while わたしの主人 is the noun phrase that gives information about 彼. の shows the relationship between the speaker and 主人.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 夫 is used, the meaning is still “my husband,” but the expression is more neutral and direct.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.tip: 主人 is often used when a wife talks about her husband; it should not always be translated mechanically as “master” or “boss.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks Bill as the person being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the car as the object of 持つ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 持っている uses the ている form to express a state of ownership.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.why: The topic ビルさんは is in a state of owning 車. 持つ changes into 持って and then combines with います to express the present state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used, the sentence only says that a car exists or is there; it does not emphasize that Bill owns it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.tip: With 持つ, to say “have” or “own,” you need to use 持っている rather than 持つ in the simple present form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vi: What time shall we have dinner?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes dinner the topic and asks about the mealtime.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the planned time for having dinner.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 何時にしますか asks about the time for deciding or arranging something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.why: 夕飯は is the topic, while 何時に asks about the time chosen for dinner. しますか creates a polite question about a schedule or decision.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only asks, “What time is it?” It does not ask when to have dinner.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.tip: に after 何時 must be kept when asking about the time for carrying out an action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vi: Is there a bag for throwing away rubbish?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks rubbish as the object of the action of throwing away.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause すてる comes before 袋 to modify the bag used for throwing away rubbish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 袋 the topic being asked about whether it exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ありませんか is a polite way to ask, often used when looking for or requesting an item.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.why: The phrase ごみをすてる comes before 袋 and modifies 袋, creating the meaning “a bag for throwing away rubbish.” Then は makes the bag the topic of the question about existence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ための is used, the purpose “for throwing away rubbish” is emphasized more clearly, and the sentence is longer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.tip: A modifying clause in Japanese comes before the noun, so you must say ごみをすてる袋 instead of reversing the order as in English.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vi: People aged three or older cannot ride this.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.sk: N（以上） + N は + N に + negative potential verb
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 以上 indicates a range beginning at age three and modifies 人.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 人 is the object being discussed, while は makes that object the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object or means toward which the action 乗る is directed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 乗れません is the negative potential form, expressing that someone cannot get on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.cn: N ＋ 以上; negative potential V
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.why: The age phrase comes before 人 to limit the people included. に goes with 乗る to indicate what the person gets on, while 乗れません expresses limited ability.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 未満, the range becomes under 3 years old instead of 3 years old and above.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 以下, the range becomes 3 years old or younger, including exactly 3 years old.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.tip: 以上 includes the stated point, so ３さい以上 also includes people who are exactly 3 years old.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vi: Please take this medicine twice a day.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Frequency ＋ Vてください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the medicine as the thing being taken.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The quantity phrase indicates how often the action of taking the medicine is performed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 飲んでください uses form て together with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.why: The medicine is the object of the action, so it goes with を. The phrase １日２回 adds frequency and comes before the request 飲んでください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: 飲みます only states the action of taking something and does not express a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 飲まなければなりません expresses the duty to take something and is stronger than a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the frequency phrase at the end of a sentence, but in this sentence １日２回 comes before the verb to modify the action of taking the medicine.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vi: I am in front of the school gate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学校 with the following noun to form a noun phrase.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects もん with 前, forming a phrase that indicates the position in front of the gate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place where the speaker exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: います is a predicate of existence for people or animals.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.why: The two uses of の connect the school to the gate and the gate to the position in front of it, respectively. 前に is a place of existence, so it combines with います to say that a person is there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: 学校のもんで would be understood as being at the school gate, without the specific meaning of being in front of the gate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 前でいます is unnatural when indicating a place of existence; with います, the location usually uses に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with います, but when indicating where a person exists or is staying, they need to use に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vi: My family also lives in Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the noun after it to show possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: も replaces は or が and means “also.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the subject exists or lives.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: すんでいます expresses the state of living in a place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.why: The phrase わたしの modifies （かぞく）, and then も marks the added information. The place comes before the verb with に, while ています expresses the current state of living there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with は, the sentence only presents my family as the topic and no longer has the meaning of “also.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as in Vietnamese in every situation, but for a place of residence, they need to remember to use に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vi: I borrowed a pencil from my friend.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who lends something or the person involved in the action of borrowing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that was borrowed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: かりました is the polite past form of かります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.why: The lender is marked with に, and the borrowed item with を. The verb is in ました form because the action has already happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the focus is on the source from which the pencil was received, closer to “from my friend” and without emphasizing the object relationship of the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 借りました is written, the structure stays the same; only the kana is replaced with kanji that have the same reading.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に and を, but に is the person who lends something, while を is the item that is borrowed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vi: I cannot go tomorrow because I have something to do.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ Vので ＋ negative potential V
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the task that needs to be done, which is the thing that exists in the structure ある.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause clause with the result that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 行けません is the polite negative potential form, meaning “cannot go.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.why: The time is presented first with は, the cause comes before the result with ので, and then the result 行けません follows. The negative potential structure expresses that the action of going cannot be performed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still states a cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行きません is used, it means “will not go,” not necessarily “cannot go.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 行けません as “will not go,” but here it means “cannot go,” not simply “do not want to go.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Jim the topic being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective つよい to indicate a high degree.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks strength as the part that has the characteristic つよい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: つよいです is an adjective predicate with the ending い in the polite form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.why: After the topic ジムさんは, とても increases the degree of the description. The pattern Nが強い describes an ability or body part with a high level of strength, so が comes before the adjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 力があります, the sentence emphasizes that Jim has strength or ability rather than directly saying that he is very healthy.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is replaced with も, it means that Jim is also strong or has strength like someone else.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put は before 力, but in this pattern for describing a characteristic, 力がつよい is the natural connection.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vi: I was startled because the phone suddenly rang.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes the adjective な 急 into an adverb that modifies the event of the phone ringing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the phone as the subject that made the ringing sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the event of the phone ringing with the reaction of being startled.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: びっくりしました expresses a reaction that happened in the past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.why: 急に comes before the noun to modify the ringing event. The cause clause ends with ので, followed by the past reaction with びっくりしました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still states a cause, but the tone is stronger and more direct.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If 急な電話 is used, 急な directly modifies 電話, and the meaning changes to an urgent phone call, not a phone ringing suddenly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 急に with 急な: 急に modifies a verb, while 急な comes directly before a noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.vi: This computer cannot use the Internet.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this computer the topic being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object related to the ability to use something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 使えません is the negative potential form, expressing that something cannot be used.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.why: The topic is the computer, while the Internet is the object related to the ability to use it, so it goes with が. The negative potential form shows that using it is impossible.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 使いません means not using it, and does not necessarily mean that it cannot be used.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate が as the English subject; in potential sentences, が usually marks the object that can or cannot be used.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vi: Lisa came to Japan last year.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.sk: N は + Time + N に + past Vます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks リサさん as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 去年 indicates when the action of coming to Japan took place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the verb 来る.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ました is the polite past form of 来る.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.why: Time is usually placed before the place and the verb to show when an action happens. 来る goes with に because Japan is the destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence describes an action taking place in Japan, not movement to Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.tip: With 来る, 行く, and 帰る, the destination usually takes に or へ, not で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vi: Because that television is broken, it cannot be watched.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes that television the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the cause, being broken, with the result, being unable to watch it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 見られません is the negative potential form, showing that watching is impossible.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.why: The sentence first gives the television's condition, uses から to state the cause, and then gives the result with the negative potential form. Placing the cause before the result makes the relationship between the meanings clear.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also indicates a cause, but it is usually softer and more objective than から.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.tip: 見られません should not be understood as simply not watching; this potential form emphasizes that watching is impossible.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vi: Please receive the card from the receptionist over there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action of receiving the card takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the source or the person giving the card.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the thing being received.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: もらってください is formed with the て form + ください, and is used to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.why: The place where the action happens goes with で, the person giving the item goes with から, and the card, as the object, goes with を. At the end of the sentence, てください turns the request to receive the card into a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Using もらいましょう makes it an invitation or suggestion to receive it together, not a direct request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に for the place where they receive the card, but で is the particle that indicates the place where the action of receiving happens.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vi: I completely forgot to do my homework.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks homework as the object of the action of doing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the action する into a noun, while を marks it as the object that was forgotten.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies わすれていました and emphasizes the degree of completely forgetting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ていました describes a state of having forgotten something and shows that the state continued until the time of speaking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.why: しゅくだいを is the part inside the action する, while するのを turns the whole action of doing homework into the object of わすれる. すっかり comes before the predicate to add the degree of forgetting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If のを is replaced with ことを, the basic meaning stays almost the same, but the tone becomes more formal and general.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.tip: You need to distinguish を after しゅくだい from を after するの; one belongs to する, while the other marks the thing that was forgotten.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形 + の + を + V
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vi: Tomorrow, please bring a pencil and a mechanical pencil as well.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time as the background for the request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: This is an item to bring and also starts the list of items.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: それに adds another item with the same function to the list.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the item to be brought.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 持ってきてください uses the てください form to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.why: は places the time first, and then the items are listed before the main action is stated. それに adds another similar object, while を marks all the items to be brought.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing それに with そして focuses more on connecting actions or events and does not emphasize adding another item.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that それに here means in addition, not an object used with the particle と.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vi: I am happy to return home, but I am also sad to say goodbye to my friends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction of the action 帰る.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the clause 帰る into a noun, while は makes returning the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects two clauses with a mild contrast and keeps a polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: と indicates the person participating in or involved in the action of saying goodbye.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: の nominalizes the clause わかれる, and then は makes it the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective さびしい acts as the predicate, and です creates a polite expression.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.why: Each action is nominalized with の and made the topic in order to express an emotional evaluation. ですが connects two contrasting emotions, while と indicates the person saying goodbye together with the speaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ですが with けれども keeps the contrast but changes the conversational tone and level of politeness.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing は with が turns the clause into the subject being described, so the contrast between the two actions is no longer emphasized.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate は in のは as part of a word, but は is actually stating the topic of the whole clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + のは
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.sk: N は + N に + negative potential V
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the time being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the class that the speaker attends.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.ch.2.n: できません is the polite negative form of the potential, expressing that attending is impossible.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.why: The time is stated first with は, followed by the class attended with に, and then a predicate expressing negative ability. This structure emphasizes being unable to attend rather than actively skipping class.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is that the speaker actively skips the class, not simply that attendance is impossible.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q26.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with 出席, but the standard expressions are 出席する or 出席できる+に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.vi: I was very nervous during yesterday's exam.
