default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the time point きのう to the noun that follows, which is the exam.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes yesterday's exam the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form, describing a state that occurred during the exam.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.why: の creates a time-modifying phrase for the exam, は marks the exam as the topic, and the predicate shows the feeling that occurred in that situation. This arrangement focuses more on the exam than on the person who experienced the feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with どきどきしました emphasizes the exciting feeling of one's heart pounding, making it more vivid than きんちょうしました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q27.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand きのうの as an independent time phrase, but の directly connects it to the noun しけん here.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds the meaning of increasing the degree or urging someone compared with the present situation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.ch.1.n: すこし indicates a small increase in amount and modifies the way of being faster.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.ch.2.n: いそいでください uses the てください form to ask the listener to hurry a little.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.why: The two adverbs come before the predicate to adjust the strength of the request. The predicate in the てください form makes the request polite rather than a harsh command.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes advice to hurry, making the request less direct.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vなさい is used, the sentence sounds like an order from someone with higher status.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q28.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place すこし after the verb, but in this sentence it comes before the verb to modify the degree of speed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.vi: I will go to visit my friend tomorrow.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the visit will take place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the friend to the noun おみまい and shows who will be visited.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.ch.2.vi: go to visit someone who is ill
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.ch.3.n: いきます is the predicate showing movement toward the stated purpose.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first. Then の identifies the person being visited, and に states the purpose before the movement verb comes at the end. おみまいに行く is a fixed phrase meaning to go visit someone who is ill.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.vs.0.d: If 会いに行く is used instead, the focus is on going to meet a friend, without necessarily implying a visit to someone who is ill.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見舞う is used, the person being visited usually goes with を, and the sentence focuses on the direct act of visiting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q29.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を after おみまい, but the pattern for showing the purpose of movement is おみまいに行く.

default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents このかばん as the topic being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 軽い is an  い-ending adjective used as the predicate to describe the bag.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: です adds a polite tone after an adjective ending in い.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.why: The bag is presented as the topic with は. Then 軽い serves as the predicate to describe its feature. です comes at the end to make the expression polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 重いです, the meaning changes to the bag being heavy.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 軽くないです, the sentence becomes negative: the bag is not light.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.tip: With an い-ending adjective, keep い before です; do not change it to 軽いだです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.vi: You need a ticket to enter here.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates a place, while は presents this place as the area or object being emphasized.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates a time; the verb before とき is in the plain form to create a time phrase.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks what is needed in the pattern いる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.ch.3.n: いります is the main predicate and expresses necessity.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first. Then the necessary item appears with が, followed by the predicate いります. This pattern expresses that an item or something else is necessary in the situation stated earlier.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.vs.0.d: If 必要です is used instead, the meaning is still necessity, but the expression sounds more explanatory and formal than いります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q30.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with いります, but a necessary item usually goes with が.

default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vi: Of the seasons, I like spring the best.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects きせつ with 中, creating the phrase "among the seasons".
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the range used for comparison or selection.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object liked the most within the stated range.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 好き is an な adjective and serves as the predicate with です.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.why: The phrase Nの中で limits the range of comparison. Then Nが presents the most outstanding object. いちばん comes before 好き to emphasize the highest degree of liking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If いちばん is omitted, the sentence only means that the speaker likes spring, without the meaning of liking it the most.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 好き, but 好きです usually goes with an object that has が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vi: A large typhoon is approaching Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place that the typhoon is approaching.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that is approaching.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 近づいています uses the ている form to describe an event in progress.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.why: N に is the place or object toward which 近づく is directed, while 台風が is the subject of the action. The ている form shows that the typhoon is currently approaching.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence focuses on the action of approaching or the intention to approach, without emphasizing the process in progress.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that the distance is becoming shorter; it does not directly describe the typhoon moving toward Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 近づく; the place or object being approached usually goes with に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vi: If you go straight along that road, there will be a bookstore.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the road being followed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 行くと connects a condition with the result that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists at the stated place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate that indicates the existence of an object.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.why: その通りを is the route being followed, so を is used. The clause 行くと comes before the result 本屋があります to express the natural result of going straight.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行けば is used instead, the sentence has a clearer hypothetical-condition meaning and does not emphasize a natural result as 行くと does.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers tend to use に with roads, but when saying to go through or along a route, Japanese usually uses を.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vi: Tomorrow, I will leave home at 7 o’clock.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + N を + Nする
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は sets tomorrow as the time reference for the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the starting time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を indicates the place left in the usage 出発する.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the polite form of 出発する and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.why: 明日は gives the general time, while 7 o’clock に specifies the exact time. うちを is the point of departure, and 出発します expresses the act of departing.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If うちから is used, the sentence emphasizes the starting point or place of departure more than the natural usage with 出発する.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate “leave home” and choose から, but 出発する can use を to mark the place left.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vi: This is a famous food in my country.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the object being introduced the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects わたし to the following noun to show possession or belonging.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the area or place where the food is famous.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 有名な is an adjective ending in な, used な to connect directly to the noun 食べもの.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べものです is a noun predicate that identifies this as a food.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.why: わたしの国で limits the place or area of evaluation. 有名な comes directly before 食べもの and uses な because it is an adjective ending in な modifying a noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 有名の cannot be used because 有名 is an adjective ending in な, not a noun that can be connected with の in this structure.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 有名に is usually used to modify verbs or show a change, so it cannot directly modify 食べもの.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit な before a noun, but an adjective ending in な must have な when it comes before a noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vi: My older brother is working in the United States.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし to the following noun referring to a person.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 兄 the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the work activity takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ている expresses an ongoing state or action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.why: わたしの modifies 兄 to show a family relationship. アメリカで indicates the workplace, while はたらいています expresses an ongoing activity.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: アメリカに usually indicates a direction or destination, so it is less suitable than で when talking about where work takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: はたらきました refers to work done in the past and does not express the current state of working.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for every location, but で is used for the place where an activity takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: My younger sister is wearing a black skirt.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person wearing the clothes.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 黒い comes before the noun スカート to modify the skirt.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the clothing as the object of はいています.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: はいています expresses the state of wearing something on the lower body.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The adjective 黒い comes directly before the noun it describes. スカートを is the object, while ～ています expresses the state of wearing it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 買っています means buying or usually buying, not the state of wearing something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 着ています is usually used for shirts or clothing in general, while はいています is suitable for skirts and clothing worn on the lower body.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use 着る for every type of clothing; skirts, trousers, and shoes usually go with はく.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.tokens.4.m: wear, put on, or put on one's feet (trousers, shoes, socks)
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.cn: Aい + N; Vて + います
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: I always buy vegetables at the greengrocer’s.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the type of goods being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies 買います and indicates frequent occurrence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: やさいは is the topic, while the place where the action is performed is marked by で. The adverb いつも comes before the verb phrase to add information about frequency.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: に with 行きます indicates the destination, the greengrocer’s, not the place where the buying takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: から emphasizes the source or seller instead of only the place of purchase.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: The place where an action takes place uses で, not に when saying “where to buy.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: Please give me one apple and one tangerine of each kind.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.sk: N と + N を + Quantity + ずつ + ください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two nouns that are both being requested.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the types of fruit as the object of ください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ずつ shows that the quantity is divided equally among each type.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.cn: Number word + 助数詞 + ずつ
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: と connects the two listed nouns, and を marks them as the things wanted. 1つずつ comes before ください to say that each type is given one unit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: 1つください can be understood as asking for only one fruit in total, so it does not clearly mean one of each type.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: づつ is an old or less common spelling; in modern writing, use ずつ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: ずつ comes after a quantity and means “each” or “every”; do not confuse it with と, which connects nouns.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 赤い modifies the noun いろ that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing liked in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 好き is an adjective ending in な, using the polite form 好きです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: Red is formed by 赤い modifying いろ. In the pattern 好きです, the thing liked goes with が, while the speaker as the topic goes with は.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence means wanting to have something, not simply liking it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 好き, but the standard structure is object + が + 好きです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: Turn right at that traffic light over there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: あそこの modifies the place or thing mentioned after it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を here indicates the point or route where the turn is made, not an object being acted on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the direction of the turn.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 曲がる is changed into the polite form 曲がります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: あそこの identifies a specific traffic light. A landmark location goes with を, while the direction of movement goes with に before 曲がります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the place is understood as the general location where an action takes place, without focusing on the turning point or route.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate word for word and use で for every location, but 曲がる usually uses を for a point or route passed through.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: I do not need this book anymore, so I put it in the box.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this book the topic of the clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the clause giving the reason to the result clause; いらない is the ordinary form of the adjective い.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates where the object is put.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 入れる is a transitive verb, changed into the polite form 入れます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The clause いらないので、 gives the reason first, and then states the action of putting the book in the box. With a verb meaning to put an object somewhere, the receiving place uses に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: ために usually indicates a formal explanatory purpose or reason, and is less natural than ので in this sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ので with ですので; before ので, the adjective い keeps its い form, as in いらないので.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ ので／Aな・N ＋ な ＋ ので
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: “What do you take to Tokyo?” – “I go by bus.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle まで indicates the endpoint of the journey.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the means of transportation, and なに asks what that means is.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きますか creates a polite question about going to Tokyo.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で marks the bus as the means of transportation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the predicate, while the subject is omitted because it is clear from the context.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: まで answers the question of where someone is going, while で answers what means of transportation they use. In the answer, バスで replaces なにで, and the verb 行きます is kept.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks about the destination or direction, not the means of transportation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for transportation, but means of transportation must use で, as in バスで.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: どうぞ is an adverb used to make a polite invitation or request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 入ってください consists of the verb in the て form and ください, and is used to request or invite someone to do something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 失礼します is a fixed expression used when asking permission to enter or disturb someone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: どうぞ softens the invitation, while 入ってください directly invites the listener to come in. The reply uses the fixed expression 失礼します to show politeness when entering.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also means “please come in,” but it is more formal and uses honorific language.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ください as only meaning “please,” but Vてください is a complete pattern for a request or invitation to do an action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes yesterday the topic or time reference of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that is in the state of being closed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 休み is a noun describing a day off or closed state, and combines with でした to express the polite past.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: 昨日は places the time reference at the beginning of the sentence. 学校が is the subject, while 休みでした describes the school’s past state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used with 学校, the school becomes the topic, making contrast or emphasis clearer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を after 学校, but the state of a subject usually uses 学校が ＋ a noun or adjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: This shop has good service, doesn’t it?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being commented on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object evaluated by いい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: いいです is the adjective predicate, describing good quality.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ね is used to seek light agreement or confirmation from the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The sentence puts the topic first with は, then states the object being evaluated with が. The adjective いい comes at the end as the predicate, while ね creates a shared-confirmation tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ね is replaced with よ, the sentence focuses more on informing the listener than on confirming something together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use は after サービス, but when saying that the service is good, サービスがいい is the natural connection.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: Excuse me, please come here for a moment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This is an opening phrase used to call the listener or attract their attention.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと modifies the request, making its tone softer and more polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 来る.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 来てください creates a polite request, in which 来る changes to the て form before ください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: ちょっと comes before the place to soften the request. こっちへ indicates the direction, while 来てください comes at the end to complete the request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If こちらへ is used, the meaning does not change, but the expression is more formal and polite than こっちへ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks whether someone may come here or gives permission to do so; it is no longer a direct request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Do not connect ください directly to the dictionary-form verb; the verb must first change to the て form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: Here is your 20-yen change. Thank you very much.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.sk: Quantity ＋ N の ＋ N です ＋ thanks
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the amount of money to the noun おつり that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: です acts as a noun predicate, confirming the money being returned.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: This is a polite expression of thanks used after a transaction has been completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: ２０円の modifies おつり to identify the amount of change. おつりです is a noun sentence with です, followed by an independent sentence of thanks.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence is used, the focus is on the action of returning 20 yen, not on naming the money as change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression gives thanks in the present or when receiving the item, while ありがとうございました is usually used after the matter has ended.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Do not translate の mechanically as “of”; here it connects the amount of money to the noun おつり.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: Kevin is the smartest person in the class.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being compared and evaluated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で limits the scope of the comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 一番 modifies あたまがいい, showing the highest degree within the class.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the aspect being evaluated in the phrase あたまがいい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: いいです is the predicate of the phrase describing someone with a good mind.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: The subject is stated with は, the comparison range uses で, and then 一番 comes before the quality phrase to create the meaning “the most.” The phrase あたまがいい uses が because あたま is the aspect that has the good quality.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning focuses on having the best study ability, more specifically than あたまがいい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: 最も and 頭がいい are more formal, but the superlative comparison structure is still similar.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for the range, but the comparison range usually uses で: クラスで一番.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.cn: N は + N で + 一番 + Aい／Aな
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I had a delicious dish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は marks the time given as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Adjective おいしい comes before a noun to describe 料理.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the dish as the object that is eaten or enjoyed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: Verb いただきます is the predicate and is a polite expression used when receiving or eating food.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The time expression is placed at the beginning and marked with は as the topic. The adjective comes before the noun, and the noun combines with を as the object of the verb at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べます, the sentence simply says that someone eats. The humble and polite tone of いただきます is lost.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that を marks the direct object. It should not be translated as “with” or “at.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: Excuse me, could you lend me your textbook?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.sk: Opening phrase + N を + Vて + ください
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This is a polite opening phrase before making a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item that is requested to be lent.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: かして is the て form of かす. It connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to express a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: 教科書を is the object of the lending action. Verb かす changes to the て form and connects with ください, so the whole sentence becomes a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the speaker asks for permission to borrow instead of directly asking the other person to lend something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a softer request in question form, while かしてください is more direct.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: 貸す means “lend to someone,” while 借りる means “borrow”; do not switch these two verbs.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: Yesterday was warm, but today is cold, isn't it?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the time or topic for comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ですが connects two contrasting clauses; あたたかい changes to the past form あたたかかった.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は shifts the topic to today.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: さむい is the adjective predicate, while ですね expresses confirmation or agreement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The sentence sets two times as topics to compare the weather. ですが connects the contrasting clauses, while ですね makes the comment softer and suggests asking for agreement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ですが with けれども keeps the contrastive meaning, but the tone becomes more formal and stiff.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the い-ending adjective to the past form when talking about a past state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: I have a cold, so I do not feel well.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the fixed phrase かぜをひく, meaning “have a cold.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ひいて is the て form of ひく. It connects the cause to the state in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the state わるい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: わるいです is the predicate and politely describes a bad condition.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The phrase かぜをひいて gives the cause first, and then 気分がわるい gives the result. Particle が goes with 気分 because 気分 is what directly has the state わるい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of ひいて, the sentence states the cause more clearly and loses the natural connecting tone of the て form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が before an adjective, which removes the relationship between the subject and the state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: Please put it a little farther to the left.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action おいてください and indicates how much farther the movement should go.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the direction or destination of the placing action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: おいて is the て form of おく. It connects the main verb with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence and turns the previous action into a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: もう少し shows the amount, 左に shows the direction, and おいてください expresses a request for the listener to place something. に is used because 左 is the destination of the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で focuses on the place where the action happens, so it is less natural than に when saying to place something toward the left.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に and で. For a direction or destination, に is usually used.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: Peter plays the piano very well.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents Peter as the person whose ability is being evaluated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action ひく.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the phrase ひく into a noun, while が marks playing the piano as the activity evaluated as 上手.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 上手です is the predicate and evaluates Peter's skill.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: Peter is the topic, while playing the piano is nominalized with の to become the object of evaluation. The pattern Vのが上手です is used to say that someone is good at an activity.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using こと instead of の can also nominalize an action, but it is usually drier and more formal in sentences evaluating skills.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ピーターさんが, but は is more suitable when stating who is being evaluated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のが + Aなです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: Last week, I visited a factory.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.sk: Time N + Nを + Vました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and shows when the action happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the factory as the object visited.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: けんがくしました is the polite past-tense predicate and describes a completed action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: The time expression is placed first to set the frame for the action. 工場 takes を because this place is treated as the object of the visit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes going to the factory, without directly saying that the speaker visited it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate “visit a factory” with に, but the object of けんがくする goes with を.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the action or sound is happening.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject making the call or sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ないています describes an action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: 外で sets the scene, 鳥が states the subject, and ないています is the predicate showing an ongoing action. This order moves from place to subject and then to action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that the speaker hears the bird's sound, rather than directly describing the bird as calling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for a place, but the place where an action happens requires で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: How about some alcohol? Then, just give me a little.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents alcohol as the topic being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: どうですか is used to ask for an opinion or whether the listener will have the item.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: じゃ is a short form of では and is used to move to a reply or decision.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: だけ limits the requested amount to a small quantity.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ください is placed at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The first sentence makes お酒 the topic and uses どうですか to ask for the listener's reaction. The reply uses だけ to limit the amount, then places ください at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 少ししかありません, the meaning changes to “there is only a little,” emphasizing limitation rather than making a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand だけ as meaning “only” in all situations, but here it limits the amount requested.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: Because I have a fever, I will go home early today.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks an existing symptom in the pattern ねつがあります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the cause before it with the action after it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes today the time range for the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 早い changes to the form 早く to modify the verb 帰ります.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate, in the polite present form used for a plan or an action that will happen soon.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and ends with から. The time and main action are stated afterward. 早く comes directly before 帰ります to show the manner or time of returning home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of から, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: からです is usually used to answer or explain something at the end of a sentence. It is less suitable than から for connecting a cause with a following action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put から at the end of the whole sentence, but when the cause comes first, から must connect directly to the result clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ から
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: I do not like fish dishes, so I do not eat them at all.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose preference or reaction is being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 魚 with 料理 to show a dish made from fish.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: With adjectives expressing liking or disliking, が marks the object of the feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: きらい is an な adjective; the で form connects the disliked state with the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 全然 modifies 食べません and usually goes with a negative form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main predicate in the polite negative form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: 魚の料理 creates a noun phrase in which 魚 modifies 料理. きらいで connects the cause or state with the result 全然食べません, while 全然 emphasizes the degree of negation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If きらいだから is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more directly and strongly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 全然食べない is casual, while 全然食べません keeps a polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use きらいなで, but the な adjective must change to きらいで when connecting clauses.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vi: Nice to meet you. I am Smith. I look forward to your support.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.sk: Fixed greeting ＋ N です ＋ どうぞ ＋ よろしく
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This is a fixed greeting used when meeting someone for the first time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: です acts as the polite predicate in a sentence introducing one's name.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: どうぞ is an adverb that makes the following words softer and more polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.3.vi: I look forward to your support
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: よろしく is the final part of a social greeting and expresses a wish for a good relationship.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: The three short sentences perform three functions in order: greeting someone for the first time, introducing oneself, and ending with a social greeting. どうぞ comes before よろしく to make the greeting more polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If どうぞよろしくお願いします is used, the request and formal tone become clearer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate よろしく as a specific verb, but it is a social expression and should be understood from the context.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q8.tokens.0.m: nice to meet you / hello when meeting for the first time
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vi: I go to the same university as my father.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who goes or studies.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: と identifies the object used for comparison in the pattern おなじ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: おなじ modifies 大学, while に marks the destination of the action 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes movement toward the stated place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: 父と provides the comparison point for おなじ, and おなじ modifies the place 大学. The particle に marks the destination, so it comes after the place phrase and before 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used instead of に, the sentence still shows direction toward the university, but it emphasizes direction more than the destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 似た大学 means a university similar to the one my father attended, not necessarily the same university.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit と in 父とおなじ, but と is required to state the object of comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vi: Because I am too busy, I do not have time to reply to emails.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 忙しい changes to 忙しくて to connect the cause with the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: メールの modifies the noun 返事 and shows that it is an email reply.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb する.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the thing that does not exist in the pattern 時間がありません.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ありません expresses nonexistence or absence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: The clause 忙しくて states the cause first, while 時間がありません is the result. The phrase メールの返事をする modifies 時間, meaning the time needed to reply to the email.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 忙しくて with 忙しいので still states the cause, but the explanatory tone is clearer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 忙しいて, but the adjective ending in い must change い to くて.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vi: I graduated from university last year.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Nを ＋ Vしました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that the topic of the sentence is the speaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 去年 indicates when the graduation happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the place or educational level from which the speaker graduated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する, forming the expression “graduated.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: わたしは sets the topic, 去年 states the time, and 大学を marks the object of the graduation action. The verb is in the polite past form because the event has been completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This form emphasizes that the state of having graduated existed before another past point, rather than simply stating that graduation happened.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: With 卒業する, learners may easily use に, but nouns referring to schools usually go with を when expressing graduation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vi: My stomach suddenly started to hurt.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.sk: Adverb ＋ Nが ＋ Aいく ＋ Vなりました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 急に is an adverb that modifies the whole unexpected change.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the body part that changes into a painful state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective いたい changes to いたく to connect with なる and express a change into a painful state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました expresses a change of state and is in the polite past form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: 急に shows that the change happened suddenly. The structure Aいくなる describes the subject changing into a new state, so いたくなりました means “became painful.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence only says that the stomach hurt; it does not emphasize a change from not hurting to hurting.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use いたいなりました; before なる, the adjective ending in い must change into the く form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: It is cold, isn't it? Shall we turn on the heater?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: ですね is used at the end of a sentence to express an impression and seek agreement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing that is turned on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう attaches to the continuative form of a verb to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: The first sentence states the weather or a feeling, and the second gives a suggestion that fits that situation. ストーブを is the direct object of つける.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: つけてください asks someone else to turn it on, while つけましょう invites the speaker and listener to turn it on together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: ましょう means inviting or suggesting that someone do something together, not simply referring to the future.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vi: Because I have not seen my family for two years, I feel lonely.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.sk: Nに + Period of time + Vていませんから + Aいです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object of the action of meeting in 会う.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ２年 indicates a period of time that continues up to the present.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 会っていませんから combines the state of not having met someone with から to state the reason.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: さびしいです is the conclusion and expresses the speaker's current feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: The 会っていませんから clause gives the reason first, and the さびしいです clause gives the feeling caused by that reason. ２年 is placed before the verb to show the period during which the speaker has not met someone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: ので can also state a reason, but it is usually softer and more objective than から.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: With 会う, the object usually goes with に, not を as with many verbs meaning “meet” in English.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: There is a cat in my house, so it is always lively.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets my house as the topic, while に marks where the cat exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists in the pattern には〜がいる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: いて is the て form of いる, connecting the cat's existence with the comment in the following clause.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: にぎやかです is a predicate adjective ending in な, describing the atmosphere of the house.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: うちには sets the scene as my house, and ねこが marks the thing that exists in that setting. The いて form connects the clause about the cat with the comment that the atmosphere is lively.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: ねこがいるので clearly expresses a cause-and-effect relationship: because there is a cat, the house is lively.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: The existence pattern uses に for the place and が for the thing that exists; it does not say うちをねこがいる.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vi: This movie is interesting. Be sure to watch it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the movie as the topic being commented on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: おもしろい is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate; よ adds a tone of informing and emphasis.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: The first sentence presents the topic with は and then comments on it with the adjective おもしろい. The second uses ぜひ to emphasize the suggestion and connects it with the pattern 見てください.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 必ず gives a stronger sense of obligation or certainty than a friendly suggestion.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use 見てください as a strong command; in this context, it should be understood as a polite invitation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vi: “How is the new house?” “It is very good.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the new house the topic of the question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: どうですか asks about the opinion of or condition of the object already mentioned.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: いいです is the predicate used to evaluate the house.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: The question puts the noun first as the topic and then uses どうですか to ask for an opinion. The answer uses とても to modify いいです and show a high degree.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing どうですか with いかがですか makes the question more polite and formal.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate どう as “how” in every situation; here it asks for an evaluation of the house.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vi: That train is a new model.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies 電車; は presents that train as the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 新しい comes before です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: The phrase あの電車は identifies the object being discussed, while 新しいです gives a feature of that object. The particle は connects the topic with the comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 新しい with 古い changes the meaning from “new” to “old.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: Do not put あの after the noun; the demonstrative あの must come before 電車.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: Children aged three and under are free.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 以下 marks an age range not exceeding three; は presents the group of people to whom it applies.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 無料です functions as the predicate and states that no payment is required.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The phrase showing age and range comes before は to identify the people covered. The following part is the noun 無料 combined with です to form a polite predicate sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 未満 is used, it means younger than three, not including exactly three years old.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse 以下 with 未満; 以下 includes the stated limit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: I will go to the vegetable shop to buy groceries.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ indicates the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun 買い物 combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes the action of moving.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The destination comes first, followed by the purpose of going, and then the verb 行きます. The two particles へ and に have different roles: destination and purpose.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に in 八百屋に行きます is still correct, but に focuses more clearly on the specific destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Do not understand 買い物に as a place; に here shows the purpose “to buy groceries.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: My house is far from the school.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: わたしの modifies 家; は presents my house as the topic for comparing distance.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から marks the reference point used to determine the distance.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 遠いです is an adjective predicate that states the distance from the school to the house.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: The sentence makes my house the topic, uses から to make the school the reference point, and then uses 遠い to describe the distance. This order matches the meaning “as for my house, it is far from the school.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 遠い with 近い changes the meaning to say that my house is near the school.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use で to mark the reference point for distance; this pattern uses から with the meaning “from.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: I can hear a strange sound from the next room.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies 部屋 and forms the phrase “the next room.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point of the sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies 音.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound that is heard with 聞こえます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞こえます describes sound entering the ears naturally, without emphasizing intentional listening.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The phrase marking the source is placed before the object that is perceived. With 聞こえる, sound usually goes with が because it is something heard naturally.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 聞きます, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker intentionally listens to the sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 音, but 聞こえる usually uses が to mark sound that is heard.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.sk: N は + いくらですか / Quantity + N です
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that bag as the topic of the question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: いくらですか asks about the price of the preceding topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The money phrase acts as a noun predicate and states the price of the bag.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: です connects the noun phrase showing the amount of money with the polite answer.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The question places the topic first and then uses いくら to ask about the price. The answer places the amount first and ends with です because it is a polite noun sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 何円ですか asks directly how many yen something is, while いくらですか asks about the price in general.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Do not read 万 as a thousand unit; 万 means 10,000, so ３万４千円 means 34,000 yen.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: The weather is bad today, isn't it?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic of the comment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object being described as the weather.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: い follows the adjective stem and forms a predicate describing a state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね adds a tone of confirmation or seeks agreement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: 今日 は limits the comment to today, while 天気 が is the subject that has the bad quality. ですね is placed at the end of the sentence to invite the listener's agreement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: でしょう tends to express a guess or mild confirmation and is less casual than ですね.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: The adjective い comes directly before ですね; do not add な after わるい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states Lin as the topic being introduced.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 会社員です is a noun predicate that states Lin's occupation or status.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: The pattern N は N です is used to introduce or identify a person's status. The occupation noun comes before です and acts as the predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 会社に勤めています emphasizes working at the company, not merely stating employee status.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: 会社員 is a compound noun, so 会社 and 員 should not be understood as two separate parts of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: Is there a movie theater nearby?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to point to a place or thing near the speaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the location where something exists or does not exist.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the movie theater the object whose existence is being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ありませんか politely asks whether that place exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: A place goes with に and comes before the object whose existence is discussed. ありませんか is a soft way to ask about absence, often used when looking for a place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: ありますか asks neutrally whether something exists, while ありませんか has a probing tone or expresses hope that it exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: In an existence pattern, the location uses に; do not use で to state where a movie theater exists.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: What is the highest mountain in the world?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the range used for comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 一番 modifies 高い and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 高い comes before 山 to modify the noun 山.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: は states the highest mountain as the topic to be identified.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 何ですか asks for the identity or name of the thing stated as the topic.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: 世 (かい) で limits the comparison range, 一番高い modifies 山, and then 山は becomes the topic of the question. 何ですか asks for the name of that mountain.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 世界にある一番高い山 points to the highest mountain existing in the world, while で emphasizes the comparison range.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: In a superlative pattern, the range usually goes with で, and 一番 comes before the adjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.sk: N には + N が + Number of people います
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: には consists of に, which marks the possessor, and は, which states the range being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who exists in a relationship with me.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: います is the predicate showing the existence of a person.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The pattern には～がいます uses に to state the person connected through possession, while が marks the person who exists. 一人 comes before います to count people.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If います is replaced with ありません, the sentence changes to mean that the person or thing does not exist.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after わたし when saying “I have,” but this structure uses には～がいます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: Maria came to Japan last year.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.sk: N は + Time + N へ + Vました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states Maria as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 去年 indicates when the action happened and can stand at the beginning of the sentence as a time adverb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of the movement action 来ました.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ました is the polite past form of 来る and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The time adverb 去年 comes before the place and verb to state when the action happened. へ goes with 来る to indicate the direction toward Japan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: に can also replace へ to indicate the destination, usually emphasizing the destination more clearly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle へ or に after a place name, but movement verbs usually need a particle showing direction or destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: This is a town with a well-developed industry.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this place the topic being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 工業 with the phrase さかんな町, showing the field being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: さかんな is a form used before the noun 町 to modify it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 町です is a noun predicate that concludes what kind of town this place is.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The phrase 工業のさかんな modifies 町, so it is placed right before the noun 町. です connects the noun 町 with the topic ここ to form a descriptive sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence directly states that industry is the field that is developing; the meaning is more specific about what has this quality.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place さかんな after 町, but a modifying phrase in Japanese must come before the noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: He is wearing a black hat.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that he is the person being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 黒い is an adjective ending in い. It comes before the noun to modify the hat.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the hat as the object of the action of putting it on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ています describes the current state resulting from putting on the hat.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: 黒い comes before ぼうし to modify the color of the hat. ぼうしを is the object, while かぶっています describes the state of wearing it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If かぶりました is used, the sentence only says that the hat was put on in the past, without stressing the current state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ～ています as always meaning “be doing,” but with かぶる it usually emphasizes the state of wearing it.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: I will go to the bank this afternoon.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.sk: N の + Time + N に + Vます
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今日 with 午後 to form the phrase “this afternoon”.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 午後 states when the action occurs and comes before a comma as a time adverbial.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the bank as the destination of the action 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is a predicate showing movement in the polite form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: 今日の午後 forms a complete time phrase, and then に shows the destination of 行きます. The subject “I” is omitted because it can be understood from the context.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: で shows where an action takes place, so it is not suitable for showing the destination of 行く.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with the bank, but 行く goes with に or へ when talking about a destination.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.sk: Adverb + N が + Vました
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きゅうに is an adverb that modifies 鳴りました and shows that the event happened unexpectedly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the bell as the source of the sound.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 鳴りました is a polite past-tense predicate meaning that the bell rang.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: きゅうに comes before the clause to modify how the bell rang. ベルが is the subject, and 鳴りました is the main predicate in the past tense.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 急に also means “suddenly,” but the kanji spelling emphasizes the written form rather than the pronunciation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake きゅうに for an adjective, but in this sentence it functions as an adverb modifying the verb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the reference point used to judge the distance.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い serves as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: The topic 学校は is placed at the beginning of the sentence. Then ここから gives the reference point for comparing the distance. The adjective い comes at the end to conclude the topic’s quality.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use に after ここ when you want to use that place as the reference point for the distance to から.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vi: I am always thinking about my family.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb いつも modifies the action that follows.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 家ぞく with こと to form a phrase referring to something related to the family.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb meaning “think.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The form ている describes an ongoing action or a continuing habit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: いつも comes before the verb to show frequency. The phrase Nのことを is the object, while Vている comes at the end to describe thinking about that matter regularly.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes thinking about a topic rather than feelings directed toward an object.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: Do not omit こと in 家ぞくのことを when you want to say “think about a matter/family” naturally.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the bag is the topic being commented on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い comes at the end of the sentence to state the bag’s quality.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: The sentence has a basic comment structure: the topic comes before は, and the describing adjective comes at the end. です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: The adjective い keeps the ending い before です; do not add な.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: I often call my older sister.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: と shows the person who takes part in the phone call.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action 電話をします.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the noun combined with する in the phrase 電話をする.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the polite form of する and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: と comes after the person who acts together or the communication partner. The phrase 電話をします describes the action of making a phone call, while よく shows its frequency.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with に, the sentence emphasizes the person receiving the call rather than the person being spoken with.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: With 電話をする, both と and に can be used, but the meanings of a conversation partner and a call recipient are different.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vi: Of these, Team A is the weakest.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the range used for comparison.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the item identified as the weakest.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 一番 modifies the adjective and creates the meaning of the highest degree within the comparison range.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い serves as the predicate describing Aチーム.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: この中では states the comparison range, and Aチームが is the selected item. 一番 comes before the adjective to form the superlative structure.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If より is used, the sentence only says that something is weaker than one specific item; it does not claim that it is the weakest.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: In the structure 一番, the range usually goes with の中で or では; do not translate が as “and”.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: Do you have a mobile phone with you now?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 indicates the time when something happens or is considered in the question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being held or carried.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the sentence into a question; ています expresses a state of having or carrying something.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: 今 is placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify the time. 携帯電話を is the object of 持つ, while ていますか asks about the state of carrying something at the present time.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ありますか, the question only asks whether there is a phone, without emphasizing that it is being carried.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: 持っています usually indicates a state of owning or carrying something, not only the action of holding it at that moment.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic being described.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 重い is an い-adjective, used directly before です as the predicate.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: The topic is first stated with は, and then the adjective い describes the topic. An い-adjective keeps its original form before です.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: They cannot be connected directly in this way; an な-adjective must drop な and use Aなです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse い-adjectives with な-adjectives and add な after 重い.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase with は as its topic is asked about its number.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 何人 is used to ask how many people there are, while ですか makes the question polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: The topic 出席者 is placed before は, and then 何人 is used to ask for the corresponding number of people. ですか is placed at the end to complete the polite question.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This also asks how many people there are, but it is more polite and formal than 何人ですか.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use 何人 for all people, forgetting that the counter for people changes depending on the context.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: I borrowed a game from my friend.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person toward whom the borrowing action is directed and also shows the source of the loan.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being borrowed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: A polite past-tense verb form expressing that the borrowing has been completed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: The lender is used with に, the borrowed item is used with を, and the verb comes at the end. This order makes clear who the source is and what was borrowed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 貸しました, the meaning becomes that the speaker lent the game to a friend.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often reverse に and を, or use で to indicate the lender.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vi: I go to work by bicycle.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means of transportation used to travel.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate, expressing going in the present tense or as a habit.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: The means of transportation comes first with で, the destination comes next with に, and then the verb 行きます follows. The two particles show different relationships, so they cannot be freely switched.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 徒歩で, the means of transportation becomes walking instead of riding a bicycle.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use で for both transportation and destinations, although the destination of 行きます requires に or へ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to live in Tokyo.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state when the desire applies.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where the speaker wants to live.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The Vます-stem connects with たいです to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning, the place of living is used with に, and the pattern たいです is placed at the end to express a desire. たい is formed by removing ます from the polite form of the verb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つもりです, the meaning leans toward a plan or intention, which is more certain than a desire.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern adds the meaning of wanting to try doing the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often keep ます before たい, but they must remove ます before adding たいです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object identified as the speaker's classroom.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 私 to the following noun to show possession.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase before です serves as the predicate and identifies what this place is.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.why: が emphasizes the place being identified, の shows that the classroom belongs to the speaker, and です connects the subject with the identifying noun at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence only states this place as the topic, so the identifying emphasis is weaker.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use は out of habit, although an identifying sentence meaning “this is exactly...” usually requires が.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vi: This handkerchief has a beautiful color, doesn't it?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects the noun phrase 「きれいな色」 with the modified noun 「ハンカチ」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 「ですね」 is used to confirm something or express a feeling, like “doesn't it?”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 「きれいな色」 comes before 「の」 to modify 「ハンカチ」. 「ですね」 is placed at the end of the sentence so the speaker can confirm the feeling with the listener.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「きれいだ」 is used, it is an independent predicate and cannot be connected directly to 「色」 in this way.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that な-adjectives must use 「きれいな」 before a noun, not 「きれいだ」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: I will take the bus at 8 a.m.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects the time 「朝８時」 with 「バス」, showing which bus it is.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 「に」 indicates the vehicle or object toward which the action 「乗ります」 is directed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 「乗ります」 is the polite form of 「乗る」, meaning to get on or travel by a vehicle.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to identify the bus. The verb 「乗る」 is used with 「に」 when talking about getting on a vehicle.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 「バスを降ります」, the meaning changes to getting off the bus.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use 「を」 with 「乗る」, but a vehicle is used with 「に」 in this structure.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vi: I think that skirt is a little short.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 「その」 directly modifies the noun 「スカート」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 makes 「スカート」 the topic being commented on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 「ちょっと」softens the degree of the following adjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 「短い」 is an adjective, and い acts as the predicate for the topic 「スカート」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 「と」marks the content that is thought or judged.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: 「思う」is the main verb and expresses the speaker's opinion.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.why: 「スカートは」states the object being commented on, while 「ちょっと短い」is the content of the thought. This content comes before 「と」, followed by the verb 「思う」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 「と思います」, the meaning is still “I think,” but the expression is more polite.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 「短すぎる」, the meaning is stronger: “too short.”
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 「と思う」before the content of the thought, but in Japanese the content must come before 「と」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」sets 「今日」as the time reference for the action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い 「早い」changes to 「早く」to modify the verb 「起きました」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 「起きました」is the polite past form of 「起きる」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: 「今日は」identifies the time, while 「早く」modifies the way of getting up. The adjective いmust change 「い」to 「く」when it functions as an adverb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「早いです」is used, it means “early,” but it cannot directly modify 「起きました」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave 「早い」unchanged before the verb, but it must change to 「早く」.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: It is hot, isn't it? Let's turn on the air conditioner.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 「暑い」acts as the predicate expressing a feeling about the weather, while 「ですね」is used to share a feeling.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 「を」marks the air conditioner as the object being turned on.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 「つけましょう」is the polite volitional form, used to suggest doing an action together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence expresses a feeling about the weather. The second uses 「Nをつける」because the air conditioner is the object being turned on, and then uses 「ましょう」to make a suggestion.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 「つけてください」, it becomes a request for the listener to turn on the air conditioner, rather than an invitation to do it together.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 「暑い」with 「熱い」; 「暑い」is used for weather and air.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vi: How much is the bus fare to the station?
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 「まで」indicates the endpoint of a route or the range of movement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」makes 「バス代」the topic whose price is being asked about.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 「いくらですか」is used to ask about a price or amount of money.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: 「駅まで」identifies the destination, while 「バス代」is the amount of money being asked about. The pattern 「いくらですか」comes at the end of the sentence to ask about the amount.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「駅までのバス代」is used, the whole phrase becomes “the bus fare to the station,” which usually needs to be placed in a complete sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand 「代」as meaning “replacement,” but in 「バス代」it means a fee or cost.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: I sometimes call my parents back home.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action of calling and shows its frequency.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: のconnects 国to the noun that follows and modifies the person being mentioned.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: にmarks the person who receives the phone call.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: をmarks the noun that describes the action performed with します.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: しますis the main predicate and describes the action of making a phone call.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: The frequency adverb comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the modifying phrase with の. にindicates the recipient of the call, while をmarks the action of 電話をします.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning changes to a call coming to the parents, so the subject is no longer the person actively making the call.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use をwith the recipient, but the recipient of a phone call must go with に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vi: I work part-time at a factory on Sundays.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: はstates Sunday as the time being discussed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: でindicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: をmarks the content of the action performed with します.
