default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: しますis the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning and stated with は. でidentifies where the action takes place, while アルバイトをしますis the verb phrase expressing part-time work.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If に行きますis used, the sentence only says that the person goes to the factory; it does not confirm that they work there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use にto indicate the place where someone is working; the location where an action takes place usually uses で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q8.tokens.3.m: blank (the character 場 - FIELD in 工場)
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: My physical condition is a little poor...
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: のconnects the noun before it with 調子, forming a modifying phrase.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: がmarks the subject that has a bad condition.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: This word modifies 悪くてand softens the degree of the poor condition.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The form てconnects this condition to the omitted following part, often suggesting a reason or an ongoing condition.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: The phrase （からだ）の調子is the subject of the condition. The adjective 悪いchanges to 悪くてto connect with the explanation or the following speech that is left unstated.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 悪いので, the sentence states the reason more clearly: because the condition is not good...
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 悪いですがis used, the nuance changes to contrast or a polite opening.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, change いto くて; do not use でafter the plain form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: I will register for next month's trip.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 来月のmodifies りょこうand identifies the trip as taking place next month.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle をmarks the trip as the object being registered for.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb もうしこみますcomes at the end of the sentence and is in the polite form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.why: 来月のcomes before the noun りょこうto modify the trip. The object being registered for goes with を, followed by the verb もうしこみます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来月のis replaced with 来月に, 来月にdoes not directly modify りょこうbut only indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit のbetween 来月and りょこう, but のis needed when one noun modifies another noun.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.vi: I feel nervous; my heart is pounding.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: This onomatopoeic word modifies するand describes the state of a rapidly beating heart.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: するcombines with どきどきto form a verb describing a nervous state.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.why: どきどきcomes before するto turn an onomatopoeic word into an expression of a state or feeling. The phrase どきどきするacts as a verb.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with わくわくする, the meaning changes to excitement and happy anticipation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate every case as worry, but どきどきするcan also express excitement.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vi: Please stand that book upright on the shelf over there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes that book the topic of the request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: あそこの modifies 本棚 and identifies the shelf over there.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows where the book is placed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 立てて is the て form of 立てる. It connects with ください to form a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.why: その本は identifies the object to be handled, while 本棚に shows where to place it. The pattern Vてください comes at the end of the sentence to turn the action 立てる into a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 入れてください, the request only asks someone to put the book on the shelf. It does not stress keeping it upright.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse 立てて with 置いて, but 立てる stresses placing it in an upright position.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to work abroad.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.sk: N は + N で + Vます omit ます + たいです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the time as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows where the action of working takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ～たいです expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます + たいです
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.why: しょうらいは puts the time first to introduce the topic. The place of the action uses で, while はたらきたいです expresses the desire to work.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this, the sentence stresses an intention or plan, not only a desire.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に with a workplace, but the place where an action takes place must use で.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vi: Please write your name and address on the paper.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the surface or place where information is written.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と connects 名前 and 住所 to make a list of items to write.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 住所 as the second item affected by 書く.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いて is the て form of 書く. It connects with ください to form a request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ください follows a verb in the て form and expresses a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.why: 紙に shows where to write, while 名前と住所 are the two objects connected by と and together serve as the content of 書いてください. The pattern Vてください comes at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced by や, the list has the meaning of giving examples. There may be other items besides the name and address.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を after 紙, but when talking about writing information on paper, the place where it is written usually goes with に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q33.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the adjective こまかい, used to create descriptive meaning.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q33.kobun.ch.1.vi: having a small-scale or detailed quality
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q33.kobun.ch.1.n: い is the ending of an い-ending adjective and completes the vocabulary form こまかい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q33.kobun.why: This is an い-ending adjective used to describe small details or separate small items. When it stands alone, the word remains in the dictionary form こまかい.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q33.kobun.vs.0.d: If it changes to 細かく, the word becomes an adverb, meaning to do something in a detailed or fine-grained way.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t18-q33.kobun.tip: Do not add だ after an い-ending adjective in the present affirmative form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vi: I will stay at my friend's house tonight, so I have quite a lot of luggage.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time and topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 友だち with 家 to create the phrase “your friend's house”.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the place where the action とまる takes place.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause clause to the result that follows; とまる uses the dictionary form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject that is described as plentiful.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.why: こんやは sets the time as the topic, then 家にとまる states where the speaker will stay. The clause とまるので serves as the reason and leads to the comment にもつが多いです.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still means “because,” but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If ため（に） is used, the sentence is more formal and objective. It is less natural than ので in casual conversation.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with a place, but the place where the action とまる takes place must go with に.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vi: Because January 1 is New Year's Day, I will go to a shrine.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the date as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is New Year's Day
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the cause with the result. After the noun しょうがつ, な must be used before ので.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction of movement toward 行きます.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.why: The clause before ので gives the reason, and the clause after it gives the action of going to the shrine. へ is used because the focus is the direction of going to the shrine.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with だから or なので, the reason sounds more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If じんじゃに is used, the meaning is still to go to the shrine, but に focuses on the specific destination more than へ.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.tip: After the noun or adjective な, before ので, な must be used. It cannot connect directly with Nので.

default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vi: My younger brother is taking care of this dog.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the dog the topic, meaning the object being cared for.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person performing the care.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: せわしています describes the care action that is currently being performed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to make the dog the topic, then uses が to identify the person performing the action. This order is equivalent to saying, "As for this dog, my younger brother is taking care of it."
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the dog becomes the direct object. This expression can be understood, but it is less natural than いぬはせわする in this structure.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is changed to the past, it means that the younger brother finished taking care of it or took care of it in the past. It does not necessarily mean that he is caring for it now.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate は mechanically as "be." Here, は only marks the topic, while が marks the person performing the action.

default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: I arrange the cups on the table.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows where the cups are placed.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being arranged.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ならべます is in the polite form and describes the action of arranging.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: The place where an object is put comes before に, while the affected object comes before を. The verb ならべます comes at the end of the sentence and is conjugated in the polite form.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 置きます, the meaning is to put down the cups. It does not stress arranging them in a row or organizing them.
default.q.speedgoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for the object and を for the place, but に is the place where the object is put, while を is the affected object.
